Xcom 2 is an awesome game and raises the bar in squad tactical combat genre.
The game has a great story line leading you deeper into the plot as you progress learning new things about the aliens and why they have come to earth.
What is unique about Xcom 2 is that your every decision has an impact on your progress to rid the aliens from earth. You will often find yourself making many value judgements of which is the greater evil or most needed benefit of multiple choices of actions. For example when you counter dark events, do you choose the dark event based on the need for what the reward offers you or do you counter the dark event based on stopping the aliens from acquiring a benefit that will make them stronger. Sometimes you get lucky and you get both. When you embark on taking down the dark event are you bringing the right combination of soldiers, experience and equipment to get the job done?
Another unique quality about the game is you get an emotional attachment to your soldiers and you find yourself picking favorites. You find some soldiers survive many missions and become powerful veterans while others look like they will last a long time only to see them killed in action. When you experience a loss you feel it in the game and emotionally.  For example, seeing your psi-op solider who just trained for a good month or more get wacked within three missions. You are not paying attention to how many turns your extraction window is and you have soldiers going missing in action. Or how about that unstoppable ranger or that long range sharpshooter who has been dealing death mission after mission and one day his number is up. This is something you must accept when playing Xcom 2 that your soldiers will fall in battle and when they fall you got to pick yourself up and move on without them toward victory.
Another unique quality Xcom 2 offers is a constant sense of urgency. You are constantly under pressure. I find myself cursing at the operations guy whenever he opens his mouth telling me the obvious. For example, you may be on a retaliation mission to save a resistance camp. On this type of mission you have to weigh the balance between speed to cover ground quickly (in order to rescue civilians which will easily expose your soldiers to enemy fire) and moving cautiously putting your soldiers in over watch as you hear alien gunfire taking down civilians during a turn. If you move too fast your soldiers may become isolated without over watch support. If you move too slowly you may have over watch support but the civilians are getting massacred.
Another pressure mission are the ones I call the “8 turn wonder missions”. You have 8 turns to hack a terminal, escort a vip to an extraction point or to destroy a data relay and all hell stands between you and the objective. Meanwhile as the firefight ensues back and forth, the ops guy pops in reminding you the short window of extraction is getting narrow. These are very challenging missions which can be accomplished but you feel pressure mounting as each turn your soldiers miss their shots, get injured and remain in the same vicinity exchanging gunfire as opposed to moving toward the extraction point.
Then there is the pressure of the avatar project. The aliens move very quickly to build the avatar project and if they are successful, then you lose and its game over. Your first assaults on the avatar facilities will be based on your efforts to make contact with local resistance groups in order to land there and blow it up. However there are only so many facilities that are found via making contact and the rest of them you have find via skulljacking advent soldiers. Skulljacking is a daunting task especially when it comes time to jack a codex. Making contact and finding these facilities Is not as easy it looks because you have to manage your intel and your supply between either:  1) improving your soldier’s weapons and gear, 2) improving the avenger or 3) expanding over world finding contacts. While you are busy hustling to gather up intel and supplies the aliens are stacking up the avatar progress quickly.
Then there are those glorious moments during the game when ambushes execute flawlessly. Your soldiers are in the right place with over watch hitting their targets. The terrain feels natural as you watch your sharpshooters take down targets at long range perching from building or hilltops. Your rangers evade enemy overwatch slicing and killing their targets on one hit. Your specialist hack those towers to gain an immediate benefit or you take control of mech unit. Your psy-op soldier takes control of an archon who then lays waste to a group of advent troops. Your skulljack attempts don’t end up costing you soldier or killing target with over watch fire as your ranger stuffs that piece of metal into an advent soldier’s skull.
Xcom  2 is a great game. If you like squad tactics using different soldiers with a variety of skills and abilities to take down enemies on many different terrains and environments with all kinds of weapons, ammo, explosives, armor and gear, then Xcom 2 is a must have game. I highly recommend it.

Ah, Trove. The single best game I have played in a few years now. That isn't saying much, because I don't play a lot of games, but... eh.
To talk of this game, the easiest comparrison I can make is to Cube World. Some say it is a blatent rip-off. I say it's everything Cube World was, but with a TEAM of devs who LISTEN to fans.
Let's get started, shall we?
PROS:
-Trove has simple, fun gameplay that isn't overcomplicated and is fun for children and adults alike.
-Every single battle has a chance to reward you, and all dungeons offer rewards.
-The game's "Loot Collector," which is a machine that converts dungeon loot you don't need into basic crafting material, or Flux, is ingenious.
-Despite this game being free-to-play, the COMPLETELY OPTIONAL purchases are either cosmetic or will help you skip work that is plenty easy to do on your own. This isn't some game that has insanely long obligatory wait times. There's a purchase-only kind of currency, called Credits, but it is used to either make purchases easier or to puchase cosmetic-only items. Not only that, but for certain Mastery levels you are awarded these Credits. And speaking of Mastery...
-Styles and Mastery. For a completionist, this game has it ALL. This game could take you WEEKS to get ALL stuff, and that isn't counting event-exclusive stuff. Every new kind of style, every new pet, every new mount/wings/boat/tome/MORE gives you Mastery points, and a certain amount of Mastery levels you up in the Mastery department. Each level-up gives you a new reward. Yeah, you need to pay money to get all the costumes and such to fll it up... OR DO YOU? Not here! There is a trade chat channel where you can buy costumes for various amounts of Flux, often around 40k at the time of this review. And speaking of trade...
-A community-hosted market. In the trade channel, you can buy pretty much anything aside from weapon, mask, and hat styles. You can also sell your product, too. And it doesn't benefit the makers, so we won't have the Trove Dev Team gettng lazy like Valve and pulling 200000000000000000000000 dollars a year off of the community market.
-ACTIVE, CARING DEVS. These devs are smart and give the fans what they ASK for, such as a more complicated endgame, and they have promised to work on a PVP system later on.
-The endgame. Thanks to the Rise of the Shadow Tower, we have a serious endgame with cool bosses such as teh Weeping Prophet and Pinata God (cooler than it sounds.)
-The Co-op. EVERY MMO EVER NEEDS THIS GAME'S LOOT SYSTEM. As opposed to dropping loot that ANYONE can grab, loot is INDIVIDUALIZED. So if an enemy drops a rare item for you, someone else can't steal it, because it ONLY shows up for you and 7 other people nearby. ANd, let's say you're mining some Shapestone. Well, for every block you break, each person gets 1 block of shapestone. WHICH. IS. AWESOME. Runescape, World of Warcraft, EVERY MMO, LOOK AT THIS GAME. IT HAS THE SINGLE BEST LOOT SYSTEM I HAVE EVER SEEN. And almost every single task in-game is benefitted from having multiple people helping, so there really is no excuse to be alone...
These are just a FEW of the pros, but if I gush any longer, I'll forget to review the cons.
CONS.
-The INFINITE number of styles. Getting 100% in this is nearly impossible... That adds to the fun, because there is always more to explore, but to someone who wants to finish this and be done, you'll be here for a while...
-Gameplay can be repetitive. There isn't any denying that the gameplay of each individual class varies, but... there is only one startegically beneficial way to play each class for the most part. And as others say, thsi makes the game very grindy to get what you want... I find this forgivable though, simply because if you get bored of grinding one thing you can grind another.
-THE TUTORIAL. Very short! Yet it also explains... next to nothing. It explains the main design and all, but this game suffers from what I call "Terraria Syndrome." Be ready to look a LOT of stuff up if you don't have a friend who can explain it! Why does every MMO ever SUCK SO MUCH...?
-OVERLY active devs...? Yeah, the servers are kinda... down... a lot. And given the lack of single-player... it kinda... sucks. But they go down for maintenance, which makes them a LOT better.
-FISHING. SO useful! You can turn 90 "Glim" (a kind of currency in-game) into 200-400. However... Fishing takes an ETERNITY...
Overall, I rate this game a 9.5 out of 10. The flaws don't detract from the gameplay enough for a significantly bad rating, despite their number...
I would reccomend this game to any and every person who saw Cube World, liked it, but either couldn't afford it or were let down by its developer. Just be ready to looks some crap up...

If you enjoyed Xcom you will enjoy Xcom 2.
Pros:
- Graphics signifigantly upgraded.
- Audio. Weapons sound great as do the strange voices of the aliens.
- Detail. The maps have various detailed aspects. When you're on a mission the maps look and feel
like their location. When you shoot near a squad mate they animate ducking to avoid the
projectiles. When an alien or enemy is missed they animate ducking or moving aside. When firing a
weapon, most notably the various heavy chain guns, if there is something in the way some of the
projectiles will hit that something regardless if you succesfully hit an enemy.
- AI. Xcom is known for being tough, particularly until you figure out strategies. For me its taking my
mind out of the casual game mode into serious thinking. Making mistakes can be very bad.
Occasionally you might get lucky and it won't affect the mission too much. The AI usually takes
advantage of your mistakes. It also is good on its own. It takes advantage of squad members close
together. It often will blow up the roof you're standing on or blow up your cover before other aliens
fire at you. There are many other ways the AI is smart and fewer where it is not.
- Tension. Choices matter. Not as in a RPG where they effect how people will relate to you, but as in
deciding what you value most in fighting the aliens. What tech to research before others. What
items to buy first. What upgrades. And so on. Despite discussion in the forums and probably in
many reviews THERE ARE NO TIMED MISSIONS. You can leave Xcom 2 running, go away for
days and your turn will still be waiting there for you. There ARE missions with a set amount of
turns before your tranpsport will have to leave and abandon the team or before the aliens'
transmission is broadcast, and so on. This is very good tension. Usually scouting ahead with
a piece of tech or one of your squadmates is very important; figuring out how to avoid detection
or where to set the best ambush.
- Overall the gameplay is fantastic. Xcom 2 is worth playing again and again. Whether you're playing
with your game set to Ironman(only one single saved game) or not and realize you've done a poor
job and need to restart to a new game Xcom 2 is just as fun as if it was your first time playing.
Cons:
- A lot of people have been reporting graphics problems. In my currently 86 hours of play time I have
only encountered graphics issues once. Not to imply that the people having graphics issues are
not. Just that I have not. I've also only CTD twice and had one or two bugs that were not game
breaking. My guess is graphics fixes will be coming eventually.
- Despite the amount of detail sometimes, while working correctly according to the rules of the game,
bullets will go through cover and hit an enemy. I think this is because in simulation the enemy is hit
due to stepping outside of cover, but you do not actually see it and the game registers a hit despite
the animation having the enemy behind cover. On rare cases I've seen aliens shoot through walls
they should not be able to. But its very rare.
- There is a particular enemy in the game, avoiding spoilers here, that has too long of a range
for its physical ability. Not because its is fair or unfair, but because its just ridiculous immersion
wise. Again its a physical ability and not psychic(something not a spoiler as psychic energy has
been in Xcom lore for a while now).
- Xcom2 for Ironman needs an option to restart a mission. I realize some might think that does not
make sense. For me I can deal with dying soldiers, failing a mission, etc. However when an entire
squad dies and leaves all of its tech on the battlefield the frustration becomes too great and the
pleasure of playing is very diminished. The tech has to be built again and as you play you're
generally on a tight budget.
- The story could be a lot more interesting.
So over all Xcom 2 is a fantastic game and you must buy it if you enjoy strategy games. 8.5/10

TLDR: Great look and feel, but RNG goes beyond risk/reward and resource management and can just screw you anyway. Seems to be building towards a long and unfulfilling/frustrating grind.
The game feels great when it seems like everything is calculated risk and resource management. If you get a disease or negative quirk from an object instead of treasure, that is fine because you know the risk and have the opportunity to abstain. If you have a character go insane from stress in combat, you likely didn't bring people capable of healing stress or brought someone you should have left in town for a round. A defeat from pressing on when you're low on supplies is also a learning experience. Essentially, you need to take steps so that even if something goes wrong it isn't game over.
Unfortunately the variance is just too high. Maybe ~11 weeks (11 dungeon expeditions) into the game, my party of 60-75% health, low stress characters encountered a boss that was not marked on the already scouted map and was magnitudes more powerful than anything else in the dungeon. The party wiped with one enemy minion left.
The problem with this is even if you take fewer risks, have an excess of resources, and the game indicates what is supposed to be in the next hall or room, you can still lose everything in a single random twist. That crosses the border from punishing to unfair.
And if this is happening so early into the game, I'm expecting there to be a lot more situations like this one.
Given that there is an achievement for finishing within 99 weeks, and the tremendous costs of upgrading anything beyond the first level in the town, I'm going to assume that this game won't be worth the time, effort, and frustration to complete.

This game is amazing. It is a refreshing and challenging take on the classic Japanese rpg (jrpg).
I wont describe the whole game, since its been a while now from its release and info on that is plenty. What I will do, is clarify a lot of the misleading reviews out there, that are drenched in emotions (mainly rage lol).
The “grind” people cry about
For starters, this game is as much “grinding” as pokemon, fireemblem, xcom, final fantasy… Its not grinding lol. Grinding is when you do something repeatedly in order to acquire or progress on a game, which does not have that Action as a main component. Simply put, fighting different trainers in pokemon, is not a grind, it is the main point of the game so you either enjoy it or not.
In the darkest dungeon, you will explore different areas and fight different creatures, with different heroes, gear them, upgrade your town and use your resources wisely. It has many different spices (like town events) to mix things up, but in the end this “grind” lol, is the whole point of the game.
Difficulty and RNG
As a gamedesigner I can tell you that, there is a difference between well placed rng and filler (cheap) rng. Cheap rng is the one you see in most tcgs, where you have no control over it and it is there to spice things up, but is usually frustrating.
Smart RNG, is the one that tells the player that, if he does X, he might get Y or W… In other words, if the player wants to interact with the coffin, he might find rewards or he might get poisoned…. This smart placement evokes the “risk over reward” idea, which is basically the vibe of this game. They even have a intro message stating “this game is about making a bad situation less… bad…”, so you can expect challenges and tough decisions, but nothing out of the blue.
The game is in fact, unfair in favor of the player… Yes. For example, when your hero gets killed, he does not die immediately, he stays in a “death’s door” debuff, where the next damage he takes, MAY or may NOT kill him… If you think about XCOM or Fire Emblem, you will remember that those games were way less forgiving.
Another fact is the amount of things the game offer the player in order for him to feel more secure towards a decision he has to make. Potions, bandages, food, buffs, %+ for almost everything, guaranteeing that your success chance is actually high. This is more than we can say about Darksouls for instance, since there is no potion in RL for twitch reflexes…
This is a thinking game and it will challenge the player like no other, because of an extremely well designed game, that forces the player to accept bad results and move on immediately. That is the roguelike spirit. However, unlike FTL (which I love) this game places really smart rngs and a continuous progression system, so the player does not have to restart the game, only take a few steps back.

If you've never played a Souls game before it might be hard to understand why they are so appealing to so many people. Why would someone want to play something that is so difficult, video games are supposed to be fun. But they're not hard because of cheap enemies or wonky controls like a retro game, they're hard because everything about them is unforgiving. Any time you die it's because you messed up, you have to learn from that and overcome the obstacle. Nothing in this game is cheap or unfair, it all comes down to skill, strategy, and keeping calm. Once you start to get the hang of it, and you start beating some bosses and making real progress, it almost becomes addicting. I can't think of any other game series where I literally jumped up and shouted like a maniac because I beat a boss that seemed impossible at first. To me, and many others, these games are the most fun because they are so deeply challenging.

If you enjoyed Xcom you will enjoy Xcom 2.
Pros:
- Graphics signifigantly upgraded.
- Audio. Weapons sound great as do the strange voices of the aliens.
- Detail. The maps have various detailed aspects. When you're on a mission the maps look and feel
like their location. When you shoot near a squad mate they animate ducking to avoid the
projectiles. When an alien or enemy is missed they animate ducking or moving aside. When firing a
weapon, most notably the various heavy chain guns, if there is something in the way some of the
projectiles will hit that something regardless if you succesfully hit an enemy.
- AI. Xcom is known for being tough, particularly until you figure out strategies. For me its taking my
mind out of the casual game mode into serious thinking. Making mistakes can be very bad.
Occasionally you might get lucky and it won't affect the mission too much. The AI usually takes
advantage of your mistakes. It also is good on its own. It takes advantage of squad members close
together. It often will blow up the roof you're standing on or blow up your cover before other aliens
fire at you. There are many other ways the AI is smart and fewer where it is not.
- Tension. Choices matter. Not as in a RPG where they effect how people will relate to you, but as in
deciding what you value most in fighting the aliens. What tech to research before others. What
items to buy first. What upgrades. And so on. Despite discussion in the forums and probably in
many reviews THERE ARE NO TIMED MISSIONS. You can leave Xcom 2 running, go away for
days and your turn will still be waiting there for you. There ARE missions with a set amount of
turns before your tranpsport will have to leave and abandon the team or before the aliens'
transmission is broadcast, and so on. This is very good tension. Usually scouting ahead with
a piece of tech or one of your squadmates is very important; figuring out how to avoid detection
or where to set the best ambush.
- Overall the gameplay is fantastic. Xcom 2 is worth playing again and again. Whether you're playing
with your game set to Ironman(only one single saved game) or not and realize you've done a poor
job and need to restart to a new game Xcom 2 is just as fun as if it was your first time playing.
Cons:
- A lot of people have been reporting graphics problems. In my currently 86 hours of play time I have
only encountered graphics issues once. Not to imply that the people having graphics issues are
not. Just that I have not. I've also only CTD twice and had one or two bugs that were not game
breaking. My guess is graphics fixes will be coming eventually.
- Despite the amount of detail sometimes, while working correctly according to the rules of the game,
bullets will go through cover and hit an enemy. I think this is because in simulation the enemy is hit
due to stepping outside of cover, but you do not actually see it and the game registers a hit despite
the animation having the enemy behind cover. On rare cases I've seen aliens shoot through walls
they should not be able to. But its very rare.
- There is a particular enemy in the game, avoiding spoilers here, that has too long of a range
for its physical ability. Not because its is fair or unfair, but because its just ridiculous immersion
wise. Again its a physical ability and not psychic(something not a spoiler as psychic energy has
been in Xcom lore for a while now).
- Xcom2 for Ironman needs an option to restart a mission. I realize some might think that does not
make sense. For me I can deal with dying soldiers, failing a mission, etc. However when an entire
squad dies and leaves all of its tech on the battlefield the frustration becomes too great and the
pleasure of playing is very diminished. The tech has to be built again and as you play you're
generally on a tight budget.
- The story could be a lot more interesting.
So over all Xcom 2 is a fantastic game and you must buy it if you enjoy strategy games. 8.5/10

Most people would describe this game as terraria in space, and in essence it is, but I find it more interesting, the game I think looks better, plays better, and in general the mechanics are better. Starbound is an extremely fun game. It has almost infinite exploration and many mods that can develop your experience in the game.
However there are some bad points, I would still recommend the game but I will say the current progression system is a bit boring, it seems tedious at the moment and once you do it once, I see no reason to repeat the process on different characters as there is no variety in the paths you can go down. It really just seems like a grind. After you have got to max tier, which solo you would be able to do in a day or two (about 15 hours of playing) and in a group you can do much quicker, there isn't much to do other than explore gather resources. But that still has a massive element of fun, and I find that to be more engaging than the actual progression system.
But currently the endgame consists of building and jumping from planet to planet exploring, which is fun, but a bit lack luster. The game is enjoyable, no doubt about that. But it doesnt consist of much at the moment. I would recommend it if you are a fan of games like terraria and minecraft, and dont mind the grind and the lack of endgame, however if not I would suggest to wait until they add more features. Despite all this it still remains one of my favourite games in my library, but right now, there isn't a lot to keep me playing.

I have to say that this is one of the most addicting and well designed games I have played in recent memory.  It is nice to see a game put together this well at release.  It IS hard, but not in a cheaty unfair way. - Nice Graphics.
- Plenty of character customization. You will get attached to your people, and many will die.
- Simple, yet challenging tactical gameplay.  Just rushing in will only get you killed.  Also, there are MANY crucial descisions that always need to be made on the world map and in the Avenger
- Its is a challenge, and really captures the essence of a deperate struggle against a much more powerful enemy.
- Open for modding.  I wont use mods on my first playthrough (I do have the two DLC's), but I am excited to see what people come up with for this game.  It's sure to be good.
Cons:
- Mild framerate drops.  This only happens in the pre and post mission sequences in the dropship for me though.  Ive got an NVIDIA GTX 980M 8GB, graphics are on high.  The alien turns hang up sometimes as well, but this is rare.
- More stats.  I like stats, so keeping track of all of the character stats would be awesome instead of just missions and kills.
I cant give you anything worse than the two minor cons above.
Overall 9.5/10

Výborná hra.
+ Atmosféra, výpravy jak v Dračím Doupěti na kterém jsem vyrostl - jidlo, pochodne, lektvary - chce to trošku strategie abyste vydrželi do konce,
+ Stejně tak to chce přemýšlet jaký tým do které lokality vezmete. Třeba charaktery zaměřené na krvacivé útoky na kostlivce asi ne =)
+/-  Někdo by to mohl počítat za záporný rys hry, ale to, že hrdinové často umírají vám dává pocit opravdovosti. Ze začatku (jako milovníka Baldurs Gate atd) mi trochu vadilo, že mi hrdinové umírají. S tím, že hra nema žádný save/load si je budete hýčkat o poznaní citelněji.
+ Hra se ukládá non-stop. Můžete ji kdykoliv vypnout a kdykoliv zapnout, hra se načte přesně na stejném místě. (platí i pro souboje atd). To dělá hru časově nenáročnou (přesto že celkové dohání časově náročné je), v klidu si dokážete užít hru i během půl hodiny.
+ Hra se dá hrát donekonečna. Pokud chcete, dá se dokončit tuším za 20-30h. Ale klidně i za 200h, 300h atd.
+/- Nedoporučil bych hru lidem, kteří chtějí intenzivní herní zážitek, a chtějí u té hry prosedět celou dovolenou (i takoví se najdou :-) . Protože hra začne být po čase dosti stereotypní. Ale těm, kdo se chtějí sem tam ponořit do temného gotického světa, s partou hrdinů procházet kobky, jeskyně a temné lesy, bude hra úchvatným zážitkem.
+ Hrdinové trpí dosti reálnými neduhy, od obyčejných nemocí a úrazů přes psychycké problémy.

This was a game that gave me a lot of frustrations. It was a game that made me think coldly but strategically as no game ever forced me to.
This game didn't force me out of my confort zone, it forced my confort zone the f*ck out of my soul!
If you like Dark Souls, strategy games, RPGs, games with permadeath... The Darkest Dungeon is for YOU. It's horrifying and beautiful at the same time. It's a MUST PLAY for those masochistic gamers that love a goddamn challenge.
You're gonna rage quit, you're gonna tilt, you will see your favorite and most well treated warriors die again and again and again... But when you kill the boss... When you make the freaking Swine King scream it's last oink... It will bring a feeling of ecstasy and adrenaline rush that you've never seen in an RPG like that before.
It does have some RNG issues, which is a part of the gameplay that you simply can't change. If there's one thing i should complain is that it's too hard. In Dark Souls you can try again and again, you'll gain experience, reflexes and will continue to grow more and more powerful until you beat the boss, but it's not like this in Darkest Dungeon. You can't afford to "Try Again" as much as you would in Dark Souls and this might intimidate new players.
But if you're reading this, thinking if it's a good idea to buy it, then let me tell you that IT DEFINELTY IS. Getting "good" at this game is a slow but awesome process that is worth buying a camera, learning video editing and post it on YouTube. If someone does that, link me to your channel, i will subscribe to you just to see highlights of someone playing this game from the start.
The final score for me is: 10/10
Loads of fun, worth every penny, i was already hyped with the game so i bought it with the DLC included, so i don't know how the original one pays off, but from what i've seen it's not THAT much of a difference, but if you like getting immersive, try to see both versions on YouTube and judge it by yourself.

Everything matches with what the game sells on the trailer.

This game is exactly what you would expect if you've played any Dark Souls games. I was so sad when Bloodborne was announced as a console exclusive but FromSoftware haven't forgot about us and gave us this gem as a last entry in the series...for now...hopefully.
Story: As always it's cryptic, open to interpretation and out there for people who put in the time to read the item descriptions of pay close attention to the clues in the many different areas of the game and the environment. We get some more information on characters from the old games while some more interesting new ones appear. Also, we get some answers to questions that people were asking from the very first game. Sadly, little to no information about my favorite character, Velka.
Gameplay: This is the main reason I would assume people play Dark Souls games for. To be challenged and that amazing feeling you get when you finally kill a boss you've been trying to beat for the past 2 hours. That hasn't changed, the bosses are amazing and frustrating, in a good way. Every boss has a tremendous amount of move sets that you have to learn if you want to overcome it and not just that but they have some attacks that are delayed, this might not seem like much but it will throw you off your game and mess with your dodge timing. A boss who does the same attacks over and over, you will get that down in just a few deaths but when he has an attack that is delayed that will be harder to overcomes since your instinct is to dodge as soon as you see him start his attack animation that you've been doing the entire fight only to realize that if you do that, it will be your demise. The designs are very well done, bosses look extremely interesting, they incite fear when they should and some of them you will underestimate by their looks only to be greeted by the iconic “You Died” screen. If you decide to not summon any phantom to help and you try to beat the bosses alone it will be a hard journey but all those hours will be worth it when you finally see that last remaining hit point get to 0 on the boss hp bar and you're left with an amazing rush of your feat that will quickly go away, it feels so good that you're almost immediately on your way to the next boss seeking that rush.
Soundtrack: Bloodborne is still my favorite out of the series but the soundtrack in this game is still amazing. Hearing the beautiful orchestral theme play out in the background as you see the boss coming towards you sets an amazing mood of action that will culminate with an even different version of the soudntrack on the second phase of almost every boss fight. My favorite is either Champion's Gravetender or Darkeater Medir.
I bought the edition with both DLCs included. Even though Sister Friede is my favorite boss fight in the game I understand why some people didn't like the Ashes of Ariandel DLC having only 2/3 new areas that look very similar to each other with only 2 bosses is underwhelming but they fixed that in the Ringed City DLC. This is what you would expect from a DLC, the areas are bigger and there's more variety in them. You have 4 bosses that are amazing, if people tell me they are better than some of the ones in the main game I wouldn't complain.
Conclusion: If you are a Dark Souls fan you wouldn't need this review to buy this game because you already know it will be good but for newer people looking to get into this know that it will be hard, everyone started out dying over and over again to the gruesome bosses or getting killed by invaders or just simple enemies that always have the potential of ending your life if you let your guard down. But it's the satisfaction that you get when you beat a boss, when you are presented with a challenge and you put in time and effort to overcome it all by yourself or with friend, it is an amazing feeling and that alone is worth it.

Once you start to get the hang of it, and you start beating some bosses and making real progress, it almost becomes addicting. I can't think of any other game series where I literally jumped up and shouted like a maniac because I beat a boss that seemed impossible at first. To me, and many others, these games are the most fun because they are so deeply challenging.

This game is amazing. It is a refreshing and challenging take on the classic Japanese rpg (jrpg).
I wont describe the whole game, since its been a while now from its release and info on that is plenty. What I will do, is clarify a lot of the misleading reviews out there, that are drenched in emotions (mainly rage lol).
The “grind” people cry about
For starters, this game is as much “grinding” as pokemon, fireemblem, xcom, final fantasy… Its not grinding lol. Grinding is when you do something repeatedly in order to acquire or progress on a game, which does not have that Action as a main component. Simply put, fighting different trainers in pokemon, is not a grind, it is the main point of the game so you either enjoy it or not.
In the darkest dungeon, you will explore different areas and fight different creatures, with different heroes, gear them, upgrade your town and use your resources wisely. It has many different spices (like town events) to mix things up, but in the end this “grind” lol, is the whole point of the game.
Difficulty and RNG

The survival elements are what you might expect from a game with DayZ's blood running through its veins: hunger, stamina, and so on. But, unlike Bohemia's game, you don't spend half your time running through the wilderness, only to find a rotten banana. Loot in Unturned is much easier to find, and it was only minutes into my first life that I found a rifle. If you never had the patience for DayZ's drip-feed of rewards, this might appeal, but it does make stumbling across a firearm feel less special.
The Minecraftian landscape is chunky and colourful, scattered with towns, military bases, and even a golf course. Here you'll find loot and, naturally, zombies. Hey, this is an indie survival game after all. They're fast and vicious, and it's easy to get overwhelmed by them. But once you've found a weapon, and built yourself a base by harvesting raw materials in the world, you'll last longer and fight harder. It's a structure you'll have experienced in a dozen survival games before, but it works.
You can play solo, but the game feels tailor-made for multiplayer. A large number of servers already exist, although there's no in-game browser yet. Teaming up with friends to battle the hordes and build bases undeniably enhances the experience, although hackers have, predictably, targeted many servers. Developer Nelson Sexton is combating these with frequent updates, as well as fleshing out the core survival and building mechanics.

You need to grind in this game. There's no avoiding that fact, so if you're one who dislikes the repetition of going to the same dungeons (or lairs) which are almost identical again and again, you most probably will not like this game.
However, if you can put that aside, it is actually quite fun. The colours are vibrant, the designs amazing, the weapons customizable, your house movable. It allows for a lot of creative potential. Think Minecraft with Diablo. The creative aspect of building (Minecraft) does not at all interfere with the hack and slash nature of the fighting (Diablo). In fact, they complement each other well when levelling up and progressing.
However, with the pros of both Minecraft and Diablo, it has the cons of both. There is no story, and the dungeons begin to repat itself very quickly. You might find yourself trapped in limbo where you are too strong for Uber 2, but too weak for Uber 3. This is where grinding takes place.
To counter that, friends really help. Get a group of your friends and go hunting, it is really very fun in that aspect. Personally, I think Trove is great for solo play to a certain extent. I don't detest the grinding, but I really think that there should be something else for people to get stronger without the continuous repetition. With friends, it really shines.

Absolutely superb turn based tactical game.
It should be called XCOM++ as it is basically just an improved and expanded continuation of the previous title. The graphics are top notch, voice acting is good, as is the character customization and modding possibilities. Storywise, XCOM 2 takes an unexpected path by making it canon that you lost the first game. This and the new stealth mechanic make the game feel fresh and new without changing the things that made the original such a great game.
My only complaints are trivial ones. There seems to be some minor bugs with display speed that 2x alt-enter solves. It would be nice if voice responses were more appropriate and held for the last applicable action. For example if you are attacked once and the attack misses, it seems wrong for your soldier to complain that, "They're all over me!" Similarly, if you are taking multiple attacks it would be nice if you took them quicker or just had a different single animation. Another trivial complaint is how height changes cost no movement points regardless of how you get there. And it seems weird when a VIP, a scientist for example, will go crashing through a window and jump down a multiple story building as if s/he were a super-soldier.
I think that's it. I am really enjoying the game so far and am looking forward to more and more customization mods in the future.

You need to grind in this game. There's no avoiding that fact, so if you're one who dislikes the repetition of going to the same dungeons (or lairs) which are almost identical again and again, you most probably will not like this game.
However, if you can put that aside, it is actually quite fun. The colours are vibrant, the designs amazing, the weapons customizable, your house movable. It allows for a lot of creative potential. Think Minecraft with Diablo. The creative aspect of building (Minecraft) does not at all interfere with the hack and slash nature of the fighting (Diablo). In fact, they complement each other well when levelling up and progressing.
However, with the pros of both Minecraft and Diablo, it has the cons of both. There is no story, and the dungeons begin to repat itself very quickly. You might find yourself trapped in limbo where you are too strong for Uber 2, but too weak for Uber 3. This is where grinding takes place.
To counter that, friends really help. Get a group of your friends and go hunting, it is really very fun in that aspect. Personally, I think Trove is great for solo play to a certain extent. I don't detest the grinding, but I really think that there should be something else for people to get stronger without the continuous repetition. With friends, it really shines.

Alright, DS3 holds a very special place in my heart because it was the first souls game I fully played through and beat. I had previously played most early and mid game in bloodborne (up to rom the spider) and played through a tad bit of early game in the first ds game. So if your looking for a review from someone who played the predocessers FIRST then keep scrolling (Keep in mind I did play through the rest of the series including demons souls afterwards). Okay so enough rambling here it goes, First off DS3 is hard, if you enjoy playing games like call of duty then dark souls probably isn't for you. That "high" feeling you get from killing someone in COD is still there but you actually have to work for it and I think thats what makes dark souls so succesful and why it has simply become my favorite franchise. In DS3 your going to come across bosses and enemies that kill you countless times which causes you to get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off and throw your controller/keyboard around your room, but if your lucky and that controller/keyboard didn't break and you perservere and defeat that difficult enemy/boss you feel like a goddamn legend its like getting a 6 man feed in COD but multiplied by 11! So before you buy this game you need to be prepared to get brutally destroyed by enemies but its the perserverance that really gets you anywhere in this game. Now with this in mind I'm going to compare this game to the prior entries in the franchise. The overall biggest change in this game is that the movement doesn't feel clunky and unfair which in the prior just felt like another barrier to overcome and perhaps one of the hardest. DS3 also has a much faster pace to it then the prior games which made me feel more comfortable taking risks, perhaps it was just the prior experience with bloodborne I had though. Although I have mentioned good things (and will be mentioning more) I wanted to bring up a con to people with previous souls experiences or people who want a game closer to the ds1/ds2 feel rather then the BB feel, DS3 unfortanutly feels much more linear then the prior installments but at the same time its not linear as in Halo campaign or most aaa titles, what I mean by this is that the game uses more bonfires then shortcuts unlike the previous 2 games in the series. I'd assume most people reading this wouldn't care about this though considering they most likely haven't finished any prior games. I want to shortly talk about the dlc before I conclude my review, for the first dlc "ashes of ariendel" I really enjoyed the snowy setting and the challenge the new painted world offered especially the final boss fight and as for "the ringed city" dlc It basicly took the tremendous difficulty of darksouls and bumped it up to 11, the dlc includes 4 new bosses which I consider all of them harder than the base game bosses and adds a lot of cool aspects to the lore/story of the game. I'm going to conclude this review here since it has essentially become an essay at this point but I appreciate it if you read through this huge wall of text and I sincerely hope that this helped you in your decision to purchase this game. tl;dr scores and tips at the bottom of the review.
Xcom 2 is not for everyone, but if you enjoy learning through failure then you will enjoy Xcom. Xcom 2 is a turn based strategy game with some mild rpg elements (earning promotions that increase stats such as "aim" "move" "hp" and gives you two perk options per level.) The appeal to the game itself is the amount of viable items, class builds, and even build orders there are to form your coherent strategy.
Xcom 2 is not a kind game, having perma death similar to games like Fire Emblem. You can not only expect to lose soldiers, but sometimes even have to sacrifice a soldier to complete an objective on time or draw fire from a vip. This is ok in a game like Xcom, as opposed to Fire Emblem, because you do not have set characters, the game provides you with an endless amount of recruits if you have the time or the resources to recruit them. The Xcom series is a series about minimizing risks, not eliminating them.
Xcom 2 provides many different types of consumables, ammo, armors, status effects, skills, psionics and classes to formulate your stategy around. The amount of variety to the game, along with the randomly generated missions, starting locations, and steam workshop support, gives the game a high replayability factor. You will end up playing the 30 hour campaign many times just because you want to try out the new random loot mod, or because you want to try out a new strategy like applying damage over time and instant death weapon mods onto every soldier after hearing that the execution chance can proc on damage over time tics.
The expansion to the original 2012 Xcom, Enemy Within, added an incentive to speed along missions and stop the prevelant, and honestly overpowered, strategy called "Overwatch Trapping". Overwatch Trapping is the idea that you would overwatch all your soldiers except one guy with high speed, and he would move up a slight amount. If you spotted any aliens, they would be killed as they ran to cover. Xcom 2 no longer incentivices you to move at a faster pace during missions, it requires you to do so. The game introduces a turn limit to many missions, usually requiring you to either kill all enemies in an area before the time runs out, or more frequently, do an objective in an area while an endless spawning horde of aliens attempts to stop you. If the mission in question is one of the "endless horde" varities, you'll have to call in your escape, and make sure that you can make it out in time (although not every soldier needs to make it out, in fact, none of them do as long as you complete the mission.) The turn limit, while being criticized by some, has the strength of forcing you to go against the earlier stated key skill of the game, risk management. Sometimes you're going to have to take a dash and risk alerting an extra pod of alines, or you're going to have to run through an overwatch. Sometimes, you might even have to leave a soldier behind to draw fire while a VIP makes it to an escape zone.
Enough about my long winded thoughts on the game, Time to get to the part people are gonna skip down to read.
Music: 7/10
Story: 6/10
Gameplay: 9/10
Graphics: 8/10
Fun: 10/10
Severity of bugs: Mainly visual bugs like doing the window breaking animation on an already broken window. Encountered a single game breaking bug in 120+ hours of gameplay even with mods in play.
Overall: 8/10
TIPS FOR NEWCOMERS TO THE SERIES:
- Don't be surprised if you lose.
- Have backup plans. A 97% shots can miss, and it is statistically possible to miss four 86% shots in a row.
- Acid grenades are the best in the game at shredding armor.
- Just because you have concealment doesn't mean you play the game like a stealth game, instead use it to wipe out the first squad you see.
- You can set waypoints using CTRL+Right Click.
- Disorient and fire have a silence effect similar to those in rpgs and mobas. Disorient and poison reduce aim (20 percent and 35 percent respectivly.)
-Know your options! If you have a 40% chance to shoot an enemy and don't need them to die right away you can always hunker down your soldiers to give them a little bit of extra defense and dodge while you get into a better position next turn.
-Don't forget to flank! A common newbie mistake is to try to shoot through full cover when you could've walked around the cover of the enemy and raised your chances of a hit and a crit by a significant margin.
- There are a couple of deceptively useful skills such as Volitile Mix, as the 2 extra grenade damage from that skill also applies to any DoTs created by that greande. Make sure to look up any possible mechanic interactions like that on the wiki.
- Don't get disheartened if you lose a soldier or the game. The game is balanced around casualties.

One time, I invaded as a Watchdog of Farron. Been a long time since I did one, and getting someone to trespass the Crucifixion Wood is real damn hard. I want that Old Wolf Curved Sword dammit!
But anyway, I stumbled upon a queer party. A Host, a Blade of the Darkmoon, and a red invader. All Havels. That's...odd, I thought. They were all sitting around a bonfire. It took me a couple of moments to realize they were engaging in jolly cooperation.
I know as a Watchdog, I probably should backstab the heck out of that Havel host. But....I couldn't. What would Solaire say if I were to disrupt such fateful encounter? No, to not join in on this itself would be insanity! So I unequipped my sword and dropped a 'Hello' carving, and thus I became part of the unlikely cooperators.
The Host seeded so that I could help him take out the Exiles. At one point, the seed ran out, and I couldn't attack the mobs. In the end, applausing and dropping 'Very good' carvings, as well as pointing him to some secret paths, are the only ways I could be of help. It was small, it was insignificant, but the 'Thank you' carvings the party threw down every now and then made me feel fulfilled.
But then, our party thinned. Above Farron Keep, the Blade made a wrong step and died by fall damage. We all saluted in honor of his service, and then moved on. At some point, we encountered those Ghru elders, and the Host had to battle it alone. Me and the red invader? We sat back, pondering on how we could help, as the Giant's Seed effect had long since ran out.
But then, a beautiful line appeared. "A Blade of the Darkmoon is summoned through concord".
We rejoiced. Finally, someone who could help our host! I looked around for the newcomer, thinking of a way to tell them that we are engaging in jolly cooperatio--
A lightning spear flew through my chest and I phased out of existence.
...welp. Typical Dark Souls.
10/10 would passive-invade again.

You can see my play history - I've put over 300 hours into XCOM EU/EW/Long War. XCOM 2 is closer to the Long War than EU. You're going to feel tired, battered, bruised, beaten, and always always always short on resources. Want to feel like you're the scrappy resistance fighting against the inevitable victory of a global force? You better, because that's what you'll feel like form moment one.
One bad move here is worse than a bad move in XCOM. Sectopods are more terrifying, Berserkers are beings of destruction, and even Sectoids are exceptionally nasty -- think Sectoid Commanders from EU/EW, only you'll see them in your first missions.
XCOM 2 is a strict improvement on most aspects of XCOM EU/EW -- the classes have more flexibility, the mission structure is wider in depth and breadth, the weapons... well the weapons are generally the same as XCOM, but that's forgivable. Psi troops, rather than feel like a minor bonus to your already crazy XCOM troopers (Really? My sniper wants to shoot everyone, not mind control one alien!) are absolutely amazing. They can learn top tier abilities on day one, and all their ablities are both powerful and relevant. The callbacks that UE/EW had to the Original XCOM (1994) are largely gone -- XCOM 2 stands it's own ground almost entirely outside it's namesake.
Even the humor is delightful! While you may find yourself cackling like a lunatic about the most perfectly staged ambush in history, there are actual moments that may take you out of the stressful situations and actually smile and laugh! As I was running through a mission, my pistol-focused sharpshooter
The storyline of XCOM 2 is the icing on the cake -- it's got the underpinings of a much deeper alien conspiracy than it shows on the surface. This harkens back to the heady days of StarCraft in stragety game story quality.
War of the Chosen only adds to the experience -- the Chosen are true villains, and the expanded content makes your soldiers feel even more like part of your team, part of your family. Making the loss of a favorite even more crushing.

and a promise of an XCOM 3 in the same line. I'll be playing XCOM 2 until that day.

After playing XCOM - Enemy Unknown, I went into this game on a harder difficulty, as various review outlets claimed the game was too easy on rookie or veteran difficulty.
After my 2nd attempt to play on Commander difficulty, I don't think the game is playable in its current state.
The two issues that plague this game are:
Inconsistent Difficulty
On my first playthrough, after completing the tutorial mission, you must complete another mission with 4 squad members before being taken to the "ship" (the main game screen). I didn't know this until after my first playthrough, but your first mission is randomly selected.
On my first run, I attempted and failed to beat the mission 4 times. Each time I thought there must be a mechanic I'm missing, or not taking advantage of, but every time we broke cover i'd lose half or more of my squad to panic or enemy fire.
It was only until the game bugged out, and the enemies stopped firing or moving on their turn, that I was able to progress.
On my second run, my mission involved destroying a monument. On the same difficulty, I completed this mission flawlessly (no dmg to my squad).
Line of Sight
I really appreciate the inclusion of a LoS movement indicator to help you on your turn, but the game completely violates my expectations when it comes to what angles the enemy can shoot at. In my few hours of play, I've lost a handful of soldiers to aliens moving in and shooting through closed doors, floors, and walls. I suspect that these objects must have been registered (but not displayed) as destroyed. None the less, on commander difficulty getting flanked can be the difference between success and a squad wipe, and being flanked in this way is simply infuriating.
I hope to come back to this review in a few weeks once these issues are patched, but I'm not holding my breath.

One time, I invaded as a Watchdog of Farron. Been a long time since I did one, and getting someone to trespass the Crucifixion Wood is real damn hard. I want that Old Wolf Curved Sword dammit!
But anyway, I stumbled upon a queer party. A Host, a Blade of the Darkmoon, and a red invader. All Havels. That's...odd, I thought. They were all sitting around a bonfire. It took me a couple of moments to realize they were engaging in jolly cooperation.
I know as a Watchdog, I probably should backstab the heck out of that Havel host. But....I couldn't. What would Solaire say if I were to disrupt such fateful encounter? No, to not join in on this itself would be insanity! So I unequipped my sword and dropped a 'Hello' carving, and thus I became part of the unlikely cooperators.
The Host seeded so that I could help him take out the Exiles. At one point, the seed ran out, and I couldn't attack the mobs. In the end, applausing and dropping 'Very good' carvings, as well as pointing him to some secret paths, are the only ways I could be of help. It was small, it was insignificant, but the 'Thank you' carvings the party threw down every now and then made me feel fulfilled.
But then, our party thinned. Above Farron Keep, the Blade made a wrong step and died by fall damage. We all saluted in honor of his service, and then moved on. At some point, we encountered those Ghru elders, and the Host had to battle it alone. Me and the red invader? We sat back, pondering on how we could help, as the Giant's Seed effect had long since ran out.
But then, a beautiful line appeared. "A Blade of the Darkmoon is summoned through concord".
We rejoiced. Finally, someone who could help our host! I looked around for the newcomer, thinking of a way to tell them that we are engaging in jolly cooperatio--
A lightning spear flew through my chest and I phased out of existence.
...welp. Typical Dark Souls.
10/10 would passive-invade again.

What X-Com 2 does right, it does wonderfully. Tons of customization, improved combat, better classes with more defined (and varied!) roles, and a sense of foreboding provided by the story which ties the experience together.

Alright, DS3 holds a very special place in my heart because it was the first souls game I fully played through and beat. I had previously played most early and mid game in bloodborne (up to rom the spider) and played through a tad bit of early game in the first ds game. So if your looking for a review from someone who played the predocessers FIRST then keep scrolling (Keep in mind I did play through the rest of the series including demons souls afterwards). Okay so enough rambling here it goes, First off DS3 is hard, if you enjoy playing games like call of duty then dark souls probably isn't for you. That "high" feeling you get from killing someone in COD is still there but you actually have to work for it and I think thats what makes dark souls so succesful and why it has simply become my favorite franchise. In DS3 your going to come across bosses and enemies that kill you countless times which causes you to get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off and throw your controller/keyboard around your room, but if your lucky and that controller/keyboard didn't break and you perservere and defeat that difficult enemy/boss you feel like a goddamn legend its like getting a 6 man feed in COD but multiplied by 11! So before you buy this game you need to be prepared to get brutally destroyed by enemies but its the perserverance that really gets you anywhere in this game. Now with this in mind I'm going to compare this game to the prior entries in the franchise. The overall biggest change in this game is that the movement doesn't feel clunky and unfair which in the prior just felt like another barrier to overcome and perhaps one of the hardest. DS3 also has a much faster pace to it then the prior games which made me feel more comfortable taking risks, perhaps it was just the prior experience with bloodborne I had though. Although I have mentioned good things (and will be mentioning more) I wanted to bring up a con to people with previous souls experiences or people who want a game closer to the ds1/ds2 feel rather then the BB feel, DS3 unfortanutly feels much more linear then the prior installments but at the same time its not linear as in Halo campaign or most aaa titles, what I mean by this is that the game uses more bonfires then shortcuts unlike the previous 2 games in the series. I'd assume most people reading this wouldn't care about this though considering they most likely haven't finished any prior games. I want to shortly talk about the dlc before I conclude my review, for the first dlc "ashes of ariendel" I really enjoyed the snowy setting and the challenge the new painted world offered especially the final boss fight and as for "the ringed city" dlc It basicly took the tremendous difficulty of darksouls and bumped it up to 11, the dlc includes 4 new bosses which I consider all of them harder than the base game bosses and adds a lot of cool aspects to the lore/story of the game. I'm going to conclude this review here since it has essentially become an essay at this point but I appreciate it if you read through this huge wall of text and I sincerely hope that this helped you in your decision to purchase this game. If you want a challenge, this game is for you. If you want a game that doesn't hold your hand, Darkest Dungeon is for you. If you love playing Bastion, this game is NOT for you.
Darkest Dungeon is a semi-rogue dungeon crawler that asks what it would really be like to be a hero in a story, movie, or game. Form a roster of heroes, each with different strengths and weaknesses, and take four of them each week to fight the horrors of the abyss. Your heroes will get hurt, they'll get stressed, they'll learn to fear the terrors they fight. Maybe your favorite hero comes back with the Black Plague, maybe he becomes Paranoid while fighting. And your heroes will die. But in death you will learn to pick up the pieces and try again.
Darkest Dungeon kicks you when you're down, laughs at you and calls your mom fat. No hero is safe, and no dungeon is "easy". The bigger the beast, the greater the glory, however; if you persevere you may just find yourself at the end of the Darkest Dungeon.

Let me clarify a thing or two:
This isn't your average dungeon crawler you're used to be able to beat with a hint of attempt.
There is a reason why they call it The Darkest Dungeon.
This game is ruthless.
This game will be rough.
This game does not care about how fond you are of your heroes.
This game hits you hard and spits at your face.
This game shows no mercy.
People DIE.
People get KILLED, even the best ones, and they stay DEAD.
Spent a fortune on gearing up your favourite healer? Doesn't matter.
He or she can die just like that.
No matter how hard you try, no matter how much gold you spend on making sure your top damage dealer or tank will not die,
They can, and will die.
Sometimes it's bad team flow, sometimes just bad luck.
Made it through one dungeon trip? You should feel lucky.
The whole game is based on a Lovecraftian idea of how miserable and insignificant humans are in the end, no matter how powerful or mighty they think they are.
Your heroes are not immortal gods or supreme power - they are disposable flesh, cannon fodder. Expendable resource.
You recruit them to your cause, level them up, take them through Hell and worse, and watch as their puny lives are ended brutally by the hands of uncomprehendable terrors of the abyss.
This game will make you feel frustrated, angry, and miserable.
You will go through triumphant, memorable moments of how you barely managed to get your expedition party out of the infernal struggle,
and you will have moments when you feel like could die from sheer frustration alone.
BUT, should you be willing to go through all the agony, the pain, the horrors and the downhills filled with casualties and losses,
You can look back, take a look at your sacrifices and difficult decisions, and say:
"I made it."
Think you're up to the challenge? Go for it.
If not, it's okay. This game is not for everyone.

At first i recommended this game. But now...
PvE, Multiplayer(coop and pvp): story and arcade mode
- Crafting requires materials like horseshoes or gel, they are not really rare, but if i want to craft not a starting weapon i need "orbs of alchemy" (there are different grades of them. Once you unlock 3-star orbs, 2-star weapons are useless, once you unlock the 4-star orbs it's time to get a full loadout made with 4-star weapons). They are sooo rare(and expensive)... Crafting is really hard because of them, but you still can't (obviously) play all the game with 0 star items. I think you have no time to complete level with boss 10 times (not only repeat boss fight 10 times, also grind to it through other enemies that can easily kill you on their own) to get orb, but it is no problem - you can buy orbs and weapons with money.
- Do you want to get super weapon? Ok you can buy it with energy, all you need is to buy energy with real money. Want a revive? Use spark of life than is even more expensive than orbs. Have no sparks/orbs/coins? Buy energy. Want to summon knight that helps you? 5 energy. Free to play? Yes. Free fun? No.
- No balance in PvP, pro players are playing vs me.
+ Events
- Events are rare and short.
[EDIT] Yes you CAN "trade" coins (happily you don't actually trade with players, it's like trading with NPC) for energy, but the energy/coins ratio is really unfair. And these aren't any special energy-trading-only coins, you need them for other things too.

- Classes fit their role perfectly and different styles are encouraged (from very mobile agressive to very static lurking). Also the new character customization options are great. However there are some minor balancing problems (Melee of Ranger too weak for the amount of risk, most of the time you can just Run'n'Gun with Shotgun for more damage)
- The rework of the worldmap need you to be more active and gives you the feeling of having more control over the given situation: You can decide to a certain factor, what you're doing and how you're doing it. (more about that later). Also different kinds of Ressources (Info, Ressource, Scientist and Ingenieurs) leave room for your approach to save the world.
- New mechanics like Armor,Melee and weapon upgrades bring some fresh air to the battlefield. Especially armored opponents require more tactical work in fights and changes your Setup and Loadout a lot.
- The new Enemies are fun to play against. Especially the Snake and ADVENT Melee need you to adapt to the situation fast
- Starting in Concealment is an interesting way to let the players feel like hidden agressors and allows for better preparation of the whole sector. Works great!
- The Basemanagment seems very well thought through. There's new buildings which fit perfectly to the game and the old buildings got a great rework. The building part feels less grindy and more impactful on your gameplan.
- The Story is dull. A modern version of "Nazi-Germany suppressing the population and experimenting with certain civilians." Haven't seen that in a while! After 2/3 of it I already had the urge to stop playing. Currently I'm in the middle of a Legendary Ironman run (Tier 2 weaponry and armor) and am not motivated anymore.
- The freedom of the decisionmaking on the worldmap is mostly illusional. It's mostly contacting the sectors to the next ADVENT Base, clear Base, repeat. That's mostly it. Also you get interrupted by Advent a lot which gets annoying really fast. After the 4th or 5th time you sit there rolling your eyes and ask yourself "what's it this time?"
- Repetitive missions already during the first playthrough. There's basically two types of Missions: First one is "Get to Point A (Hostage, Hack Terminal, Collect Information), then go to Point B (Extraction)". Even the special missions where you locate and collect storyobjects work that way. The second type are the missions known from XCOM 1: Rescue Civilians. Just more difficult since the aliens prioritize them more and there are less. Didn't find them interesting in the first part, here aswell. Also hidden enemies in those missions. Why?
The last point is the dealbreaker for me. Even when every other part of the game got really really well refined, the lack of different missions in XCOM2 made it boring very fast for me.

XCOM is back and aside from a few annoying details, it's better than ever.
Virtually every area of the game has seen an improvement in some way. The strategic layer, combat, classes, soldier customization, enemy AI, enemy variety, mission variety, maps, resource management, all improved. But optimization and overall polish has definitely taken a hit, and there are a few questionable decisions that hold it back from being perfect.
On the strategic layer back at the Avenger, managing your base's allocated space has seen a pretty drastic overhaul, and the new contact system replaces the satellites of previous games. In general, you have a lot more control over what missions you take and what you spend your time doing, instead of always passing the time by scanning for activity like in Enemy Unknown. Now as different scanning opportunities pop up with all different kinds of rewards, you can proioritize which place you'd like to take the Avenger to scan based on the rewards that each location gives out.
As far as managing your space goes, the new upgrade system is a welcome improvement over EU. Now you don't need to wait until late-game to get the most out of building generators, for instance. When you unlock the next level generator that increases output, you can just upgrade the generators you have. It's a system that punishes you for early building considerably less than EU did. In addition, each facility can now be staffed with engineers, which are a resource that you'll gather over the course of the game. Staffing facilities gives different bonuses depending on each facility, and you can switch up which facilities are staffed on the fly to focus on what you need at any given time.
Combat is much the same as EU and EW, with some subtle refinements and UI improvements here and there. Grenades and explosives are more powerful and more important now, as you'll often fight armored enemies who need to have that armor shredded by explosives before they become vulnerable. Verticality plays a larger role now as the new maps are built more with setting up for height advantages in mind. The procedural map system works brilliantly and honestly feels like these maps were handcrafted.
Each of the replacement classes for the classes from EU is a step up from the last game, and each one has two distinct paths of skills that almost make each side feel like their own class. The Ranger replaces EU's Assault class, and can be specced for stealth melee or a shotgun vanguard. Sharpshooter replaces the Sniper and be specced for pure sniper or as a gunslinger (a pistoleer that actually has distinct advantages over a sniper -- I once took shots at 8 aliens in one turn using the Faceoff skill that lets you take a free shot at every enemy in range). The Specialist replaces the Support and can be set up as either a field medic or a hacker, and comes with a drone that allows him to heal or hack remotely. The Grenadier replaces the Heavy and can be either a demolitionist focused on explosions or a heavy machine gunner that focuses on the usage of miniguns. And there's a fifth class this time around, the Psi Operative can be acquired earlier in the game than Psi troopers of EU, and is its own distinct class with tons of great abilities. My favorite is being able to permanently mind control one enemy per mission. And the best part of all of these classes is that you can mix and match skills from both sides of each class, so you have a lot of freedom in builds.
Soldier customization is great. You have a lot more control over how your soldiers looks, with customizable faces, names, nationalities, bios, props like shades, headbands, bandannas, headgear like hoods and helmets, full control over weapon and armor color, you can add patterns to weapon and armor (and might I add, weapons and armor can be customized separately), you can pick variants armor torsos, arms, and legs (except for the  middle tier of armor -- you can't change the torso there for some reason) and can even upload your characters to a global character pool so the people you've created will appear in future playthroughs. One big missing feature: If you save a character, you can't load that appearance/description onto a rookie, you just have to hope you bump into that soldier again randomly if you want to use him. To that end, I refrained from using the character pool and will just manually recreate my soldiers next time if I want to re-use those characters. But you can also create characters to be engineers, doctors, or bad guys if that's more up your alley. And finally this one is to Firaxis (thanks for reading, Jake): Give us some more helmets, please. Such a great selection in EU and EW and yet there's only a handful in XCOM 2, and they don't look so good.
Now for some negatives: The game is not optimized well. At all. Back at the Avenger it's  not uncommon for dips down to 10-20FPS, and I have a capable rig playing on reasonable settings. I had better performance on missions after the initial ten-second stuttering as the map first loads, but many people have terrible performance all around. Here's hoping Firaxis addresses this in a future patch and manages to make this game more playable for more folks. It's unacceptable that a game in 2016 that was delayed and made exclusive for the PC runs this poorly, especially when the visuals, while ultimately good, are nothing crazy. There are also frequent hitches like the game hanging in between turns, actions taking longer than they should to start/stop playing, UI and sound bugging out. It's hard to understand why the game shipped like this when Firaxis generally knocks optimization and overall polish out of the park.
Mission timers. Oh boy. Mission timers are a divisive topic within the community. Some people love them, some people say they ruin the game, some people don't care much either way. I played on normal ("veteran", as it's known in-game) and won my first campaign, and on normal the mission timers are very tolerable. On higher difficulties however, the general consensus seems to be that they're only there to force you to rush and make mistakes. I definitely agree that they're artificial difficulty at best and while they didn't bother me so much at my difficulty level, if I had the choice, I probably would have disabled them. They didn't detract much from the game, but at the end of the day they didn't really add anything.
Wounds. My biggest gripe with the game. Injuries for your soldiers are much, much more prevalent this time around than they were in EU. If a soldier takes any hit, no matter how strong their armor is, and no matter if they get healed with a medkit, they're wounded. Wounds come in three flavors, lightly wounded, wounded, and gravely wounded. Grave wounds last up to an in-game month, and while this isn't so bad in the early game, by late-game you're going to be on missions where high-ranking soldiers feel almost mandatory to counter what you're up against. There's a facility where you can staff an engineer to cut recovery times in half, and even then the amount of time your soldiers spend wounded is obscene. The EU system of soldiers only being wounded when they take more damage than their armor adds to their health was much, much better, and I hope this new system is addressed in a patch.
Negatives aside, the game that we got is pretty much just EU but bigger and better in every way. It's not perfect, but what is? It's got some problems, but what doesn't? I would still wholeheartedly recommend this game to anybody, especially people who liked Enemy Unknown.

I'm going to give you a no BS summary of the game, straight facts, its up to you to decide what is a pro and what is a con. Afterwards I will give you my personal opinion so you can see my thoughts. Good? Good.
1.Permadeath
2.Unforgiving
3.Quick Recovery
4.Any situation can go bad fast
5.Very Difficult
6.Slight Learning curve
7.Heroes are temporary
8.All dungeons are different
9.Randomized each expedition
10.Many Classes
Those are most of the things that I'd say someone looking to buy the game would need to know. Now for my personal opinion which will be detailing my reasons for loving the game, which will be followed by a short story about when I  realized how much I loved the game.
This game is fun, it hurts, its dark. All reasons I like this game. You can walk down a hallway and if one of your heroes is at low health and he just so happens to be the one to step on the hidden trap then that's it. Chances are he's dead lying in a corridor. There goes your favorite Highwayman! You can build your party anyway you want. Just because that bounty hunter sucked when you bought him doesn't mean he has to suck forever. With a little luck he'll survive an expedition or two, and with a little gold you can get him the skill you want him to have. The fun of this game is the learning all of the small things as you go, and then when you think you know what you're doing and you're in the clear you get attacked and your entire party slaughtered. This game is brutal and not for perfectionists or those that are easily frustrated. This game will frustrate you, it will throw you through emotional loops, and it will give you a challenge. But that is the fun part isn't it? Now for a story.
I asked my friend if this game was worth getting and he said yes, but be careful, there is a guy that randomly appears and is impossible to fight, just run. So I played the game for two days and forgot about this warning. So I went on a scouting mission in the ruins with a team of new heroes, hadn't even played as 2 of the classes. About 2 rooms in this weird Eldritch phantom guy shows up. He's called The Collector. I'm like, who the hell is this guy, I've been here 20 times and never seen him before. So I start fighting. No big deal at first, he has 70 HP, and then he summons a whole party. He summoned a Vestal and 2 Highwaymen. At first I was like, okay, that shouldn't be a problem, just some random summoned creatures, like the Apprentice necromancer. But then, they started doing some real damage to my heroes. It was at that moment I realized that I was fighting what my friend had warned me about. I started getting a bit worried then but kept fighting, I managed to kill their Vestal with Flambard my Hellion, after killing their healer I picked off their Highwaymen and managed to get a few good hits on The Collector. After that fight I was quite proud, I had been scared but managed to fight a creature most experienced players were scared of and win. Keep and mind i had only been playing for 5 hours or so. Immediately after I managed to get into a fight, and my team was slaughtered ruthlessly by some undead. The only one to escape was my Hellion, who is most treasured hero. Oh wait, she was slaughtered on her next expedition by a spider.
Take my story and learn from it, you can be amazing, but it has a price. You can be confident, but it has a price, hell you have to pay to suck at this game. It is the greatest game I have played in a long time. It is hard, it will anger you, but it will teach you some great life lessons. So go stab♥♥♥♥♥♥ go kill things, go get killed, but most importantly, have fun doing it, I'm the Dankest, I mean Darkest Dungeon.
