X-Com 2 is a good game. I have 47.8 hours in it and I've just finished the game on Commander difficulty.
I have given a negative score for the game because I had expected much more from X-Com 2...
Pros:
1. Definitely improved graphics. New GPU Shaders added. All alien species are remodelled, textured and some new species added. They look awesome. Also your units, customized weapons, amor etc they look shiny.
2. There are wide variety of aesthetic customization options of your units. You can customize the appearance of their armor, weapons, hair, facial hair, scars, eye glasses, tattoos etc etc.
3. Your strategy on the campaign map is affected less by randomness compared to X-Com EU. In X-Com EU if you are very unlucky, then no matter how good you play, you may lose the game on higher difficulties. This is less random in X-Com 2 and your strategical decisions matter more.
4. Armor mechanics implemented. Armor actually reduces damage and does not only provide hitpoints. You need to remove enemy armor with grenades or with gunner skills before damaging them.
5. You can now carry your wounded soldiers out of the battle zone.
6. Slightly better physics. For instance you can destroy floors with explosives and all aliens on that floor falls on ground taking damage.
7. The most important addition I think is that missions are now randomly generated. I have not seen a map in the game which repeats itself yet.
Cons:
1. UFO fighting on air completely removed. I agree X-Com EU implementation was not brilliant. But I didnt expect Firaxis to remove this as it was an integral part of all X-Com series starting from UFO-Defense and X-Com terror from the deep.
2. You can hack robotic enemies, turrets and consoles in the game. Hacking can give you temporary or permanent bonusses. However the way you do it is really uninteresting. I mean it is no different than a Psi soldier taking control of an alien. We just have a slightly better looking interface for it. You have two options for robotic enemies. Either you stun them (just like a Psi Soldier stunning an enemy) or you may control them for 4 turns.
3. Performance issues. A SSD, a good graphics card and high RAM mostly reduce the effect. However loading times are considerably longer than X-Com EU. Also whenever you reveal an enemy group in tactical missions you get a 1, 1.5 second lag spike.
4. Replayability of the game is very low. No second wave options are unlocked after you finish the game. Ironman mode is much more difficult than X-Com EU such that even in Veteran Ironman (One higher difficulty than Rookie) my entire team wiped out many times and I failed missions. Having researched all of the technologies and autopsied all aliens in my first run I have no intention to replay the game from the start. I've tried Veteran ironman but since it is impossibly hard compared to X-Com EU, I gave up.
5. Most of the missions are time based. If you run out of turn time you lose the mission. This makes Ironman considerably harder.
6. Some enemies are overpowered. For instance Brain Cortexes can teleport and flank you in one turn and in the same turn shoot you. This means the survival of your units are sometimes irrelevant of your tactics. No matter how good you play, in Ironman mod be prepared to lose your best units due to stupidly overpowered enemies. The same goes for Avatars as well.
7. The health pool of your enemies are radically high during mid game and late game for all difficulties above rookie.
8. Although the game is difficult parametrically, the AI is stupid. You'll encounter many enemies which will not kill you when they have the chance.
9. Wounded units take very long time to recover. And no matter how large your units' health pool is, taking 3-4 bars of damage in a mission will cause a unit to become gravely wounded. It will take at least a week before they become operational again.
10. Aesthetic customization options and variety is good. But equipment customization of your units is very weak. Firaxis had removed one tier of armor and weapon sets from the tech tree of the game. This is completely random and I fail to understand the logic behind it. You may have the intel and supplies... but if you are out of luck, you cannot improve/customize your soldiers with new equipment. The same goes for experimental research. For instance to learn new types of ammo and grenades you need to carry out experimental research in proving grounds facility. However what you get from this research is completely random. Once you discover an item with this research only 1 piece is added to your inventory and you need to do the same research to get another ammo/grenade/armor type that is again random.
11. The game is very expensive considering the new stuff it brings to the table.
I must say that buy X-Com 2 only if you are a fan of the series. For now X-Com EU with the long war mod is much better than X-Com 2. And I hope most of the above mentioned issues will be fixed with mods. Until then stick with the previous game.

Three major problems exist in this game that are highly frustrating and ruin what is otherwise an enjoyable and interesting game.

If you are the kind of person who likes Darkest Dungeon, you'll like Darkest Dungeon. However, if you are the kind of person who doesn't like Darkest Dungeon, you won't like Darkest Dungeon.
Isn't that just delightfully vague? Alas, it is oh so true. It's art style, narrative bend, party management system, and peculiar tactical perspective are all the type of thing that can only be appreciated by a particular type of person. But if you are that type of person? Boy howdy. What a FUN game.
So how do you know if you are that type of person? My first suggestion would be to just buy and play it. It's cheap, and definitely worth giving it a chance if you like it or not. Otherwise, let me ask a few questions.
Do you enjoy the theme and atmosphere of the game? Darkest Dungeon relies HEAVILY on these characteristics, so if you don't care for them, don't buy it.
Are you a patient gamer? This game is complex, and requires time and thoughtful planning to enjoy. Its intricacies are not immediatly apparent.
Still here? Sweet! Let me send you off with a few thoughts.
Unlike what some folks think, this game is not all that unfair. It uses RNG, so at some point the odds will be stacked against you. But that's part of the game. If you are patient, and come to understand its mechanics, you will soon find yourself winning nearly every battle with an indestructible team of dungeon-crawling champions. I promise you, tactics and planning are pivotal. RNG is not resting upon Sheogorath's throne while plucking flower petal's and chanting, "Should I kill him? Should I kill him not? Should I kill him? Should I kill him not?"
TL;DR
It's a well made game, but not for everyone. Check first to see if you enjoy its theme, and if you are patient enough to handle a complicated game. It's not as unfair as it is made out to be.

Game is pretty challenging, but a bit underwhelming at parts (due to the lack of difficulty), but the hard part is actually navigating through most of the areas. Bosses are really well made, even the easier ones have an amazing atmosphere which compensates for the lack of difficulty. I personally beat the game for about 55 hours, but thats because I did tons of exploring and roaming around the old areas to see what I missed, but overall the game should be max 45 hours if you're gud enough.
Sadly, I can't rate it too high. The the problems are not much, but they do matter when coming all together. First off are the weird bonfires (I'll not go into detail, just experience it to yourself lul). The optimization is quite bad, some areas I can't surpass 40fps at all even though I can say I have a beefy PC (Dragonslayer Armour and the area overall was the worst, even on the lowest graphics settings it didn't make even a slight difference, so consider that if you're running on a slower of a pc, its quite a heavy game despite its looks). Another thing is how the story was told to the player, well it actually wasn't. You have to learn it yourself by reading item descriptions and making weird conclusions to explain it to yourself, but the easier way to do it is to just pass an area and then read a bit online about it. I personally didn't understand almost anything of the story until I read it online, but after I did so my vision towards the game changed a lot, in a good way. The port to PC is kinda bad. So just to skip you the pain, here are the more important controls: E to choose something from a menu, Q to go back from something in a menu, you need to go to the settings menu on the esc to close the game, you parry with left ctrl and you use your "special weapon skills" with ctrl, or shift + right click + left click (in that order). Other things are pretty minor that won't affect you at all, like the lack of hairstyles on character cration, not being able to upgrade armor and other micro stuff like those.
So as a final, i rate it 8/10. Amazing game, but its obvious that a lot of things could've been made better.

For the storyline, for the gameplay as a whole, fantastic. Well executed and diverse. Attention to detail, passion was weaved into this game, a worthy final sendoff for the series. It's everything you know and love about Dark Souls with *most* previous problems improved upon or solved.
The multiplayer, from my experience, seems to be heavily influenced by luck. Of course, skill and practice with your favourite weapon and specific skill investement can certainly guide you toward more victory, but when you're faced with a mindless R1 spammer, or magic exploiters, or any exploiter for that matter, you will discover that there were too many loopholes for people to figure out to gain a significant, mindless, easy advantage against anyone they face.
It's obvious to ignore the trolling children with their "you're just terrible at the game tbh" comments, for the above statement is factually part of this game.
The worst part being, that anyone can do it. Currently the multiplayer duel scene is over-saturated with the same weapons and builds for the sole purpose of winning, instead of skillful fun. Hackers are a thing, but rare for most.
In terms of mechanics, as stated earlier, *most* issues are solved. The main problem you'll experience and hear people talk of is the desecration of poise. Simply put, in previous games, heavier armour = sturdier defence, you couldn't be thrown off your feat or staggered easily if you put the stat investment into effectively wearing these armour sets.
Now it's seemingly gone and functions in a niche, hard-to-grasp way. Most of the time a full set of armour may feel the same as a loincloth. Many players have found themselves benefitting more from investing their equipment carry weight stat into something else, such as more stamina or health.
Conclusively I'd say this game is worth a buy, but don't get upset when you experience the problems mentioned above, for they are part of this. Consider them a small, ugly truth amongst an otherwise beautifully-crafted experience.

This is the most generic free to play shooter I have ever seen.
This can either be a good or a bad thing in your opinion so I'll just go down the list of what I've noticed -
The Good -
-Solid Graphics.
-Guns That Actually Have Recoil
-Good Gun models and overall textures.
-To further that, Graphics are solid if nothing special.
-Guns handle well and aiming is smooth.
-High Frame Rates.
-No pay to win elements (yet) Everything except cosmetics can be grinded towards by playing.
-For now, a large player base.
-Multiple classes with various capability.
The bad -
-Sniper Rifles are Overpowered, easily one shotting and instant aim.
-This unbalance makes assualt rifles and SMG's basically useless.
-This also applies to OP shotguns, all or most one shots.
-Maps are very basic, and have lots of long corridors making the sniper issue worse.
-Absolutely nothing original or fresh, really.
-Very slow grinding.
-Limited selection of weapons per class, most classes having at max 4 or 5 choices. Some only having 1 or 2.
-Derived gameplay. If you have played AVA, you have played this. It is basically just a slight upgrade that runs better.
Overally I got bored with this game very quickly. I played for a couple hours at most and was completely uninterested in it.
It is highly lacking in content with very few choices as far as weapons go, with some very clear winners in each category that make the other weapons completely obsolete.
Such as the HKN Assault rifle and the Type 95 absolutely dominate. They do higher damage than all the other assault rifles (45) and while they kick like a mule compared to the others, their time to kill is brutal with a 2-3 shot kill (If you get a headshot, it is two shot kill). The G36 is also in a similar class at 35 damage per shot, which also promises a 3 shot kill body shot and a 2 shot kill with headshot. Though it trades raw damage for a bit more accuracy and control. If you hit limbs in can potentially be a 4 shot killer too, so less reliable. Or of the opponent has heavy armor, it can be more.
Whereas the other Assault rifles tend to have less recoil but have far less damage per shot (Varying from 27 to 33) and results in far more 3 and 4 shot kills meaning the top 3 damaging rifles outclass them overall .
It is a similar theme for the SMGs (Though there aren't many). There are only two, but the clear winner is the Kriss Vector that while slightly less mobile and with a slightly lower rate of fire, has a much harder hitting shot (28 versus 22) meaning the Kriss will always be a 4 shot kill max even with a silencer. Whereas the MP7 has to hit 5 times (Due to armor protection lowering damage further), 6 if you are silenced.
Same with the LMGs. You have two choices. One is clearly better, MK46 is better in most regards to the PECHENEG. The MK46 sacrifices two damage per shot (32 versus 34). That 2 damage could be useful in theory for the PECH if the target wasn't wearing armor, allowing it a 3 shot kill instead of a 4 shot kill. But in practice everyone wears armor and both are a 4 shot kill to the body, 2 shot to the head. In reture for doing 2 damage less however, the MK46 is more stable, is more accurate, has a higher rage of fire, and greater mobility.
The sniper files are the same way.
You have 4 choices. 3 semi-automatics that are 1 shot headshots but 2 shot body shots. You start out with a semi-auto that is pretty much no different between the other 3. They are useless compared to the other rifle.
The other rifle is a bolt action sniper rifle that is a one shot chest or head shot. So unless you are an amazing headshot guru you won't be needing the other rifles.
As far as shotguns, they are both brutal but again one is slightly superior - The KSG. Both are pump action, but the KSG does so much more damage, nearly 50 Percent more, and no one is really concerned about the recoil of a pump action that corrects itself before the next shot nor accuracy because you are using it at close range only.
So to sumarize -
-Smooth performance and tight controls.
-Large player base.
-Good Graphics for a free to play.
-Quality modeling for weapons and textures.
-In Game changeable silencer is kind of cool.
-No pay to win model.
-Does exactly what it sets out to do: Make a Free to Play Shooter that is smooth and good looking to mimic smoother gameplay of modern AAA shooters.
-Absolutely nothing special and generic in everyway.
-Highly unbalanced weapons of which there are clear winners in every category.
-Shotguns and sniper rifles absolutely dominate and frustrate SMG, AR, and LMG users.
-Minimal content to unlock, many weapon types have 2-3 choices.
-Heavy grinding to unlock anything through gameplay. You earn 400 to 1000 "gold" per match for the average player. Most weapons cost between 96000 and 192000 meaning for the average player (, 750 gold per match) that means to unlock any single gun or piece of equipment you would need to play between 130 and 256 games for each and every weapon.
-Very boring and has no features as of yet that would really bring me back to it after a couple horus with better choices.
Overall I feel this game would have been very successful if the free to play market wasn't so overrun with generic military shooters already and it had more content.
However in its current state and with essentially no feature being unique in any way, I cannot really recommend this game.
Though the caviet to that - It is early access so I will keep an eye on it.
Hopefully they will add more content, create better maps, and add some features that make it stand out.

Game is pretty challenging, but a bit underwhelming at parts (due to the lack of difficulty), but the hard part is actually navigating through most of the areas. Bosses are really well made, even the easier ones have an amazing atmosphere which compensates for the lack of difficulty. I personally beat the game for about 55 hours, but thats because I did tons of exploring and roaming around the old areas to see what I missed, but overall the game should be max 45 hours if you're gud enough.
Sadly, I can't rate it too high. The the problems are not much, but they do matter when coming all together. First off are the weird bonfires (I'll not go into detail, just experience it to yourself lul). The optimization is quite bad, some areas I can't surpass 40fps at all even though I can say I have a beefy PC (Dragonslayer Armour and the area overall was the worst, even on the lowest graphics settings it didn't make even a slight difference, so consider that if you're running on a slower of a pc, its quite a heavy game despite its looks). Another thing is how the story was told to the player, well it actually wasn't. You have to learn it yourself by reading item descriptions and making weird conclusions to explain it to yourself, but the easier way to do it is to just pass an area and then read a bit online about it. I personally didn't understand almost anything of the story until I read it online, but after I did so my vision towards the game changed a lot, in a good way. The port to PC is kinda bad. So just to skip you the pain, here are the more important controls: E to choose something from a menu, Q to go back from something in a menu, you need to go to the settings menu on the esc to close the game, you parry with left ctrl and you use your "special weapon skills" with ctrl, or shift + right click + left click (in that order). Other things are pretty minor that won't affect you at all, like the lack of hairstyles on character cration, not being able to upgrade armor and other micro stuff like those.
So as a final, i rate it 8/10. Amazing game, but its obvious that a lot of things could've been made better.

UPDATE: Three Rings Design went under (quite the shocker, I know) and had the game transferred to Grey Havens, a team of ex-OOO employees who took over with no limitations from Sega on what they could and couldn't do. Sounds like the game will actually recieve content updates, right? Well, at first it kind of did, a few steps in the right direction, a bit of polishing and bug fixes, simple stuff. But just when the playerbase was starting to regain their faith in the game, the dreaded box promos returned, and returned again. The game went from a possible state of ressurrection to right back down the same exact ♥♥♥♥ing pattern of "updates" that players are sick to death of.
Having played this game for over 3,000 hours on Steam alone (about another 50 or so before the Steam release) I can say this game is nothing like it used to be. It's basically a MMO dungeon crawler inspired off of The Legend of Zelda and to be quite honest it has some serious potential, and still does.
Unfortunately the developing company (Three Rings Design or "OOO" for short) was bought out by Sega at one point and since then, the game started to decline. This decline quickly turned from bad to worse once its lead developer, Nick Popovich, resigned from OOO to pursue a living as an indie game developer. Before his resignation he had announced some major changes to the game that would be very welcoming to players both new and old and this was about 2 years ago. To this day, only a small fraction of these changes have been implemented into the game and production of new content has virtually ceased.
Any updates that come to the game come in the form of prize boxes, only purchasable with real cash and contain accessories and costume pieces that provide no benefit whatsoever other than "Wowie I got the same helmet I already have 38 others of but now in a slightly different shade of red." Every time a "new" prize box is released which at this point is almost every 2 weeks, it's nothing more than a simple change of colors for the exact same items. And the cherry on top of this whole ordeal is in the off-chance that these boxes contain an item never before seen with unique stats (such as a shield or a weapon) they have insanely low drop rates and pretty much force you to spend hundreds of dollars on boxes for a small
at it or purchasing it from another player who will more than likely have a price tag on it large enough to make you cringe.
Personally, I find the game's PvP community to be the most toxic I have ever seen, comparable to League of Legends. This is just my experience, though. The game's PvP system is a whole other wall of text I could spend days writing about.
Other than those points, I still find the game quite enjoyable to play when I have some friends to play with, and I also livestream it on Youtube every now and then which brings some of what's left of the game's good part of the community together for a good time, which is my goal. With friends to play with, the game is still pretty decent if you can get past its broken crafting system. Most veterans that have been around this game since its beta days would really hate to see it get shut down, but with the dev team leaving everyone in the dark and not saying anything about what they intend to do in the long run, it has left most of us to believe that the game's days are numbered.
TL;DR Do I recommend the game? Yes only if you have friends to play with or want to try something new. As far as sticking around and playing actively, don't even bother unless things pick up with the people in charge behind the game and its development shows signs of well... actually being developed. But in its current state, the game's future does not look too bright so if you're looking for a new MMO to get into, steer clear of Spiral Knights (for now)

The reason I didn't write a review for this game a while ago was, I didn't know what to write. I love this game, but it's hard to put how interesting it is into words.
Starbound is NOT a ripoff of Terraria, though often that is one of the first impressions people get. Like Terraria, it is an Indie Sandbox game with crafting, bosses, etc. However, there are some major differences. Starbound has a huge array of different enemies, put together from a few sprites to make random and sometimes funny-looking enemies. In Starbound, it is a little bit more on the surviving and exploration side, with LOADS of structures and strange blocks to fin, and strong enemies. Ores are more scarce. Starbound has many races to play as, each with their own pros and cons. There's too much more to talk about...
For an early access game, Starbound is amazing. AMAZING. I agree with the devs: "Starbound is already extremely playable and contains a vast amount of content". For an example, take the sheer amount of different planets. Here's the rundown:
5 sectors (galaxies)
A LOT of star systems
Each star system has 1 - 8(?) planet clusters
Each planet cluster has 1 - 4 different planets/asteroids to land on
There's so much content. I would highly reccomend this game to people who enjoy games with the option, but are not totally created around the ability, to build cool stuff. People who enjoy games that have the RPG feel of "I need to get better! I need the best stuff! To defeat all the bosses!" will enjoy this game.
20/10

I don't like that they charged for settlement enhancement stuff. Seems like they cut content and put it behind a paywall.
Automatron and Far Harbor were worth the money though, and so was the base game.
While it lacks an awful lot in the role playing department compared to the other titles, it has a faster paced playstyle and the survival mode is very nice. So if you're more into action than rpg then you'll like this one better.
RPG:
This was the biggest disappointment I had for the game. Where in other titles you could pretty well be whoever tf you wanted to be, this one pretty well rail-roads you into being Nate/Nora. You aren't a kid who grows up into whoever you want, you aren't a random vault dweller, you aren't just some random guy who took a high paying courier job, you are a family man/woman with a tendency to be an overacting drama queen. You can't keep that to yourself either, most of the time if it's the subject of discussion it's the only way forward.
Which brings me to the next complaint; There's only ever four choices to make in conversation and most of the time it's 1. Yes, 2. No, 3. [Persuade/Intimidate], 4. Maybe/[Sarcasm]. That sounds like it's a little simple but still functional, but 2, 3 and 4 are all just to stall. 1 is the only choice that makes the conversation move forward. So the only real choice you're making is "How much time do I want to spend talking to this person?"
I also dislike the voiced protagonist tbh. I know this is subjective but I liked doing my own character voice. Not every character would sound the same. But then again it doesn't matter because you don't make your own character, you just decide what Nate/Nora looks like.
Weapons/Armor:
Excellent. I really liked the crafting system in this game and I thought that the way you can mix/match and upgrade armor peices was cool. I also loved the mods for the weapons. Simplified everything and it's a lot more rewarding than just repairing items with other items all the time. Although I was disappointed to find you couldn't change what class your armor was (light, sturdy, reinforced, etc.).
Combat:
Fast paced, streamlined (almost), and rewarding. The only complaint I have here is that health scales with level instead of endurance with a DT/DR check. Which leads to people and zambies with no helmets getting shot in the face like 3+ times without dying. Damage sponges don't belong in an fps unless the player character is also a damage sponge. I suppose in the regular modes of the game it works but on hard and survival it's ridiculous. I also think power armor was a little weak. It's basically a walking tank suit, right? I just don't think the combat is very balanced on Survival for a mode that's supposed to be more realistic/immersive.
Survival:
This is Fallout 4's reimagining of "Hardcore" mode from Fallout: New Vegas. Honestly, they did this a lot better than Obsidian. The way you can collect water and cook and such is great. It also gives you more of a reason to do settlement stuff. The illnesses were a nice mechanic as well and I enjoyed the challenge of only being able to save by sleeping. Made the stakes much higher and thus combat that much more rewarding. The damage spongey-ness of the enemies made it really frustrating at higher levels though. If damage caps, so should health.
V.A.T.S.:
The V.A.T.S. has also changed. Now it just slows down time a little instead of all the way. Doesn't really give you the same level of focus imo. They should just make it a slow time effect imo since they're headed toward an action direction anyway. But that's just my opinion.
Graphics: Turn down your shadow render distance to medium. Trust me. In a city you will drop to like 13 fps if you don't. Other than that, I think the graphics are great. It's a little... softer than the last two titles. Not necessarily better, just different. Both are good imo.
Overall, I think this game is worth getting. Almost everything I complained about can be fixed with mods. Just make sure you get the season pass because you'll neeed all the dlc for most of the really important ones.

For the storyline, for the gameplay as a whole, fantastic. Well executed and diverse. Attention to detail, passion was weaved into this game, a worthy final sendoff for the series. It's everything you know and love about Dark Souls with *most* previous problems improved upon or solved.
The multiplayer, from my experience, seems to be heavily influenced by luck. Of course, skill and practice with your favourite weapon and specific skill investement can certainly guide you toward more victory, but when you're faced with a mindless R1 spammer, or magic exploiters, or any exploiter for that matter, you will discover that there were too many loopholes for people to figure out to gain a significant, mindless, easy advantage against anyone they face.
It's obvious to ignore the trolling children with their "you're just terrible at the game tbh" comments, for the above statement is factually part of this game.
The worst part being, that anyone can do it. Currently the multiplayer duel scene is over-saturated with the same weapons and builds for the sole purpose of winning, instead of skillful fun. Hackers are a thing, but rare for most.
In terms of mechanics, as stated earlier, *most* issues are solved. The main problem you'll experience and hear people talk of is the desecration of poise. Simply put, in previous games, heavier armour = sturdier defence, you couldn't be thrown off your feat or staggered easily if you put the stat investment into effectively wearing these armour sets.
Now it's seemingly gone and functions in a niche, hard-to-grasp way. Most of the time a full set of armour may feel the same as a loincloth. Many players have found themselves benefitting more from investing their equipment carry weight stat into something else, such as more stamina or health.
Conclusively I'd say this game is worth a buy, but don't get upset when you experience the problems mentioned above, for they are part of this. Consider them a small, ugly truth amongst an otherwise beautifully-crafted experience.

So, after putting a lot of hours into all of the Dark Souls games ( mostly Dark Souls 1 and 3 ) i decided to write a review about this awesome game! Dark Souls 3 is the third and possibly the last Dark Souls game in the franchise, and frankly, it is a worth end to the series. Now let's talk about some aspects of the game.
The Story
Ever Since Gwyn has linked the first flame, there were countless other heroes that relinked the first flame so that the age of fire can continue. The three main Lord of Cinders ( SPOILERS : or rather i should say four, if you count Lothric as a Lord of Cinder. I personally don't, because he never actually lit the first flame ) rise from their grave because the fire is threatened. These lads are supposed to re-link the flame so the age can continue, but instead of doing that, they would rather watch the flame die out. So the flame ( or..rather the Bell of Awakening? i don't know ) wakes up the Unkindled. You are one of these unkindled ash. Your job is to bring the Lords of Cinders back to their thrones. Either Alive or as Ashes. My overall opinion of the story is that its pretty awesome, but can be really confusing sometimes..and it needs a lot of reading. Some portion of the story isn't actually there, you have to theorise.
The Gameplay
Dark Souls 3's gameplay is basically Dark Souls 1's gameplay, but with a lot of fixes and balances ( and some ♥♥♥♥ups xD )
You still have the same main stats, but some of them either got removed, or they were made into one stat ( Endurance no longer gives you more equip load. Instead, equip load can be raised by spending points in Vitality.  And also, the Resistance stat from Dark Souls 1 is completely gone, you can't invest points directly into resistance ) Also, because of a lore aspect, you no longer have the option to stack up Humanity. Actually, Humanity is quite gone from this game, instead you use Embers to restore your link to the other worlds and also give you an HP boost which lasts as long as you're alive. ( To Simplify it , once you use an ember you can be invaded, but you can also summon other people to help you at certain areas ) Summons ( also Invaders ) also have the option to use Estus ( although the overall Estus you can use while being summoned is reduced ) Now you can also equip up to four Rings! Quite better than just two rings. Oh and one other thing, Poise is completely broken. Covenants also return, and quite frankly some of them are really fun and they give you good rewards, and some of them are totally dead. For example, The Blade of the Darkmoon ( my favourite covenant from DS1 ) is utter♥♥♥♥♥♥♥in this game, since you can't level up, because the covenant itself relies on another covenant ( Way of Blue ) which is a completely dead covenant on levels above 25 SL. Also in this game, as my good friend Jack would say " Medium Roll actually works ". In DS3 medium roll still has the same Iframes, but now your character recovers much faster at the end of the roll. Overall , the gameplay is pretty cool, you have a lot of variety in Magic Stuff ( Pryomancy, Offensive or Healing Miracles, Sorceries , Dark Sorceries/Miracles/Pryomancies ) and you also have a ton of Melee weapons to use. This makes DS3's replayability INSANE, because you can literally make *ALMOST ANY KIND OF BUILD* you want.
Controlls
I highly recommend using a controller. 'Nuff Said. I think the controlls are good, but if this is your first Souls experience, you gotta get used to it first.
The Graphics, Areas and Armour
This game is super gorgerous! It looks amazing in almost every area! I especially love how Irithyl looks like, with all that snow and stuff. Superb! I really like how some weapons got some extra details ( Boss Weapons look amazing! ) The enemies are also very nicely detailed. Almost all of the areas look very cool, but honestly there were some areas that could've been bigger and better detailed. For example, the Profaned Capital is a joke. It's basically a 5 minute run to the boss and that's it. The Armour in Dark Souls 3 is really good! There are a lot of armour from DS1, for example you can get Lautrec's armour..or Artorias's armour ( Sadly Lord Blade Ciaran armour didn't make it into the game ) You can do a lot of cosplay by combining other armour pieces together. Overall they have a lot of variety.
Some things i wanted to mention as either cons or pros
*SPOILERS*Dark Souls 3 continues DS1's and DS2's trend with having some ridicolously easy bosses. Wolnir, Deacons of the Deep, Crystal Sage and the Anchient Wyern are basically a joke. Dark Souls 3 also continues the other trend from the other games, which is that the main guys you are supposed to defeat are probably one of the easiest bosses. The Abyss Watchers themselves aren't so hard, Yhrom the Giant is a complete joke. Aldrich isn't so particularly hard either. Although thank god the Twin Princes actually manage to put up some kind of challange. I would've enjoyed if most of these bosses put up some kind of challange *SPOILERS ARE OVER*
Also, there are the Invaders. I myself don't have a really big problem with invading, but some people really don't like how some of the community handles invading. Some invaders tend to come to you, use gestures and get you to do an Honor Duel, which is cool. Some invaders particularly like hiding behind enemies and gank you while you're trying to defeat the enemies so you can kill the invader. Overall, yeah, the community isn't perfect, but hey, that's not the game's problem. You can easily punish these invaders by using a Seed of a Giant Tree, or you can ♥♥♥♥ with them some other way too.
Alright, I think that covers most of what I wanted to say. Let's gather the cons and pros
Pros :
-Fitting end to the Series
-Lore is quite interesting
-Awesome gameplay mechanics
-Good variety of magic or pure melee weapons
-INSANE ammount of builds. You can almost make any kind of build you want.
-Graphics are awesome
-LOT of throwbacks to Dark Souls 1.
-Forgot to mention, this game has an amazing soundtrack!
-Most of the bosses are really well done gameplay,detail and lore wise.
-Can be played as coop game almost entirely.
-DLCs are pretty cool ( i'll try to write a review about the DLCs later on )
-PVP
-Lot of NPC questlines
Cons :
-*SPOILERS* the main Lord of Cinders were pretty easy to defeat. Yhorm the Giant was pretty dissapointing.
-Some areas in the game got very little ammount of detail. The Proned Capital had some potention, but it was completely wasted.
-FromSoftware, where is my Ciaran armour??
-Poise sucks♥♥♥♥♥♥ It's broken. It does not work.
-♥♥♥♥ Covenant farming.
-Blade of the Darkmoon is utter♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
-The insane ammount of lag in PVP. People can literally hit you with a broken straight sword 3 meters in front of you. I don't know if PVP is designed that way or not, but they definitely should do something about it.Sometimes you land a huge hit, and the enemy easily rolls through it, despite the fact that seemingly you hit the dude in the nuts.
Final Verdict : 9/10. If you already have completed Dark Souls 1 ( and loved it ) i definitely recommend you to purchase Dark Souls 3! If you have not yet played any kind of Souls game, its still worth to pick up, but you'll need some time to get used to it. This is an awesome end to this series! I would also like to give a shoutout and a huge thanks to my good old friend Jack for introducing me to the Souls franchise and playing every DS from the beginning to the end, and to REAPER for those cool NG+6 rage moments
Thanks for reading, peace out lads!

Three major problems exist in this game that are highly frustrating and ruin what is otherwise an enjoyable and interesting game.
1) The costs for removing afflictions and reducing stress are FAR too high. No one enjoys throwing 50-75% of their earnings into a gold-sink mechanic after every dungeon.
2) Battles and game mechanics in general are too reliant on RNG. No matter how well made your decisions are in battle, you are regularly put to your knees by crits/dodges/resists and other such nonsense. RNG is fine, but it needs to be used in moderation if the player wishes to maintain some sense of control.
3) If you level a character quicker than  you complete dungeons, he becomes useless as he refuses to enter a dungeon that is a level below him. There are several mechanics that the devs could have implemented to stop high level characters farming dungeons. Simply making a character unusable and forcing you to draft a newbie is frustrating as hell.

If you are the kind of person who likes Darkest Dungeon, you'll like Darkest Dungeon. However, if you are the kind of person who doesn't like Darkest Dungeon, you won't like Darkest Dungeon.
Isn't that just delightfully vague? Alas, it is oh so true. It's art style, narrative bend, party management system, and peculiar tactical perspective are all the type of thing that can only be appreciated by a particular type of person. But if you are that type of person? Boy howdy. What a FUN game.
So how do you know if you are that type of person? My first suggestion would be to just buy and play it. It's cheap, and definitely worth giving it a chance if you like it or not. Otherwise, let me ask a few questions.
Do you enjoy the theme and atmosphere of the game? Darkest Dungeon relies HEAVILY on these characteristics, so if you don't care for them, don't buy it.
Are you a patient gamer? This game is complex, and requires time and thoughtful planning to enjoy. Its intricacies are not immediatly apparent.
Still here? Sweet! Let me send you off with a few thoughts.
Unlike what some folks think, this game is not all that unfair. It uses RNG, so at some point the odds will be stacked against you. But that's part of the game. If you are patient, and come to understand its mechanics, you will soon find yourself winning nearly every battle with an indestructible team of dungeon-crawling champions. I promise you, tactics and planning are pivotal. RNG is not resting upon Sheogorath's throne while plucking flower petal's and chanting, "Should I kill him? Should I kill him not? Should I kill him? Should I kill him not?"
TL;DR
It's a well made game, but not for everyone. Check first to see if you enjoy its theme, and if you are patient enough to handle a complicated game. It's not as unfair as it is made out to be.

I don't like that they charged for settlement enhancement stuff. Seems like they cut content and put it behind a paywall.
Automatron and Far Harbor were worth the money though, and so was the base game.
While it lacks an awful lot in the role playing department compared to the other titles, it has a faster paced playstyle and the survival mode is very nice. So if you're more into action than rpg then you'll like this one better.
RPG:
This was the biggest disappointment I had for the game. Where in other titles you could pretty well be whoever tf you wanted to be, this one pretty well rail-roads you into being Nate/Nora. You aren't a kid who grows up into whoever you want, you aren't a random vault dweller, you aren't just some random guy who took a high paying courier job, you are a family man/woman with a tendency to be an overacting drama queen. You can't keep that to yourself either, most of the time if it's the subject of discussion it's the only way forward.
Which brings me to the next complaint; There's only ever four choices to make in conversation and most of the time it's 1. Yes, 2. No, 3. [Persuade/Intimidate], 4. Maybe/[Sarcasm]. That sounds like it's a little simple but still functional, but 2, 3 and 4 are all just to stall. 1 is the only choice that makes the conversation move forward. So the only real choice you're making is "How much time do I want to spend talking to this person?"
I also dislike the voiced protagonist tbh. I know this is subjective but I liked doing my own character voice. Not every character would sound the same. But then again it doesn't matter because you don't make your own character, you just decide what Nate/Nora looks like.
Weapons/Armor:
Excellent. I really liked the crafting system in this game and I thought that the way you can mix/match and upgrade armor peices was cool. I also loved the mods for the weapons. Simplified everything and it's a lot more rewarding than just repairing items with other items all the time. Although I was disappointed to find you couldn't change what class your armor was (light, sturdy, reinforced, etc.).
Combat:
Fast paced, streamlined (almost), and rewarding. The only complaint I have here is that health scales with level instead of endurance with a DT/DR check. Which leads to people and zambies with no helmets getting shot in the face like 3+ times without dying. Damage sponges don't belong in an fps unless the player character is also a damage sponge. I suppose in the regular modes of the game it works but on hard and survival it's ridiculous. I also think power armor was a little weak. It's basically a walking tank suit, right? I just don't think the combat is very balanced on Survival for a mode that's supposed to be more realistic/immersive.
Survival:
This is Fallout 4's reimagining of "Hardcore" mode from Fallout: New Vegas. Honestly, they did this a lot better than Obsidian. The way you can collect water and cook and such is great. It also gives you more of a reason to do settlement stuff. The illnesses were a nice mechanic as well and I enjoyed the challenge of only being able to save by sleeping. Made the stakes much higher and thus combat that much more rewarding. The damage spongey-ness of the enemies made it really frustrating at higher levels though. If damage caps, so should health.
V.A.T.S.:
The V.A.T.S. has also changed. Now it just slows down time a little instead of all the way. Doesn't really give you the same level of focus imo. They should just make it a slow time effect imo since they're headed toward an action direction anyway. But that's just my opinion.
Graphics: Turn down your shadow render distance to medium. Trust me. In a city you will drop to like 13 fps if you don't. Other than that, I think the graphics are great. It's a little... softer than the last two titles. Not necessarily better, just different. Both are good imo.
Overall, I think this game is worth getting. Almost everything I complained about can be fixed with mods. Just make sure you get the season pass because you'll neeed all the dlc for most of the really important ones.

I'll start by saying I'm really enjoying this game and don't regret getting it, however I don't reccomend buying it at full price in the state that it's in. If you can get it cheaper then go for it, provided you're a fan of EU/EW. XCOM 2 is more of the same, with a bit of different. There's a lot of good here and a lot of bad, but the bad is fixable, it's just that it shouldn't have been there to begin with.
Pros:
-The new base management and overworld stuff is pretty fun and in my opinion makes it feel like you're not just sitting and waiting for something to happen. Instead of having to try to manage a bunch of "feal levels", but only being able to affect one at a time, there's only one meter to worry about, and there are multiple ways to manage it. Having to make contact with different countries instead of having to prevent losing them gives you a bit more option as to how you approach things.
-The new/updated classes feel a lot more balanced and interesting. Each one having two distinct specializations makes your squad more diverse, however a couple of them do feel underpowered, specifically the scout and combat hacker trees.
-The weapon changes make things a lot less tedious in some aspects, but moreso in others. Pistols on the sharpshooter class are fantastic, they're decently powerful and give your sniper a way to fight in close quarters and able to attack/overwatch after moving. Being able to attack or move after reloading is just great, so taking away secondaries on all the other classes doesn't really hurt.
Meh:
-Turn timers, I know people are so divided on these which is why I put them in meh instead of cons, but I dislike them. I feel that they force you to play a certain way, even if you don't want to. I've had missions where I had to rush through enemies or else I wouldn't make it in time, causing me to risk my soldiers. There are already lots of mods to change how they work, whether it be increasing turns, reducing the amount of missions that use them, or outright getting rid of them.
-concealment adds a nice way to setup ambushes, however in most cases it doesn't work out like you think it would. This ties in to turn timers, in that the timers are counting down even while you're trying to set up your ambush. It's just not viable to try to tactically ambush the enemy when you have to get to the evac zone in 8 turns. Also having all enemies suddenly just know where you are when you break concealment can easily lead to you being surrounded if you're not careful.
Cons:
-Performance issues out the♥♥♥♥♥ Supposed to be patched.
-Glitches out the♥♥♥♥♥ Supposed to be patched.
-I don't know if it's a glitch or just poor design, but line of sight is just super wonky. I've had enemies attacking me through walls, stun lancers meleeing people through the floor above them, and worst of all, snakes pulling my guys through as many as three walls with no holes or windows in any of them, effectively dooming them.
-The difficulty curve is steep. Really steep. Within 5 missions I was fighting against armored enemies that could destroy my cover, incapacitate my troops, and almost kill them in one attack, while I was still researching t2 weapons and armor. Enemies pop up randomly one after another, giving you almost no time to adjust your strategy.
-Dodge. If that's not specific enough, most enemies have a chance to dodge, causing you to do greatly reduced damage. I know the discussion of rng has been done to death, but sometimes it feels like they just always dodge.
-Your soldiers' wounded level seems to be completely arbitrary. Soldiers that take 10% damage get gravely wounded and are out of the fight for a month to recover 2 hp. I've read of people having soldiers take over 50% damage and only being lightly wounded, but take 2 fall damage and be gravely wounded.
Hopefully they can patch the performance and glitches, with that I'd say it's worth it, but until then no. Other than that it's up to you whether these things bother you or not.

This is my first review ever for a game well deserving of it. I like to keep it simple instead of writing a full story so I will just make a quick list with pros & cons:
Pros
---
• Great gameplay. Fast gameplay where good timing is the key.
• Good graphics.
• ULTIMATE GOOD MUSIC.
• Awesome locations. The world in this game is just so dark and scary yet so beautiful.
• Incredible bosses and enemies.
• Fun to replay a few times. I finished the game with 8 different characters now and got 1 character past newgame +5.
• Great DLC. DLC 1 wasn't really that big sadly but the second was well worth every penny.
• Aside from a few problems I will mentions at the con list, the multiplayer is fun.
• A thrilling hidden story.
Cons
---
• For me this isn't really a con but you must be patient. You'll probably die a lot in this game since it's pure trial and error. I've just seen many people hating games like this for it.
• Many abilities like lots of magic and also certain weapons that are weak or even useless. When you PVP in this game most guys that turn out to win are quality builds (characters who use STR and DEX) and use fast melee weapons. Also magic is just slow they need to buff it somehow.
• The summon system. Sure it's part of Dark souls and I get why, I also know this game is more meant to play solo then with friends and yet it's really annoying sometimes to play this with friends since it's kinda hard to stay together. I wish games like these had a more fun way to CO-OP.
• They should put more attention on the LUCK stat. In the beginning you get to pick a class, I would recommend picking either pyromancer or knight since they have the lowest luck stat which is a GOOD thing, luck is really useless unless you run a few certain things.
WHY DO I RECOMMEND THIS GAME?
---

With 180h on record, I can't say I disliked the game.
The new reciepe model is a great addition, I really had pleasure tinkering around and playing a bit with defence setups for settlements. It probably is responsible for a significant part of my playtime, the other part being obviously a vast world to explore and a lots of sidequests to keep you busy. Without revealing too much, there are very interesting twists taking place in the main quests that surprised me.
But I also had my disappointments, the game really seem to push you into a big end battle whatever side you take and regardless of your skills, I would have loved to have a pacific end solution that didn't involve destroying opposing parties. What made a very long playthrough also almost bored me out but I stopped following some lengthy side quest just in time before that happened, but still I had already aa feeling of seen it all before I managed to get to one of the first possible endings. Additionally, I'm disappointed not to have the satisfaction to influence the epilogue (video at the end about the future of the wasteland) which is very similar regardless of your choices during the game in the main quests, that's a shame seeing this was, to me, of Fallout's trademarks. That gave me a cheap feeling, really...
To conclude, Fallout 4 is an honest game, there are innovations to the series and I saw the work done to the details in the game. But there are also some shortcuts to what made it a great game. If I have to recommend a Fallout game to someone, this one will only be second to my favorite: New Vegas.

Overall spectacular game.
If I had to describe it briefly, I would say that it"s turn-based Dark Souls.
Darkest Dungeon brings an entertaining mix of challenge and fun. The gameplay is extraordinarily difficult, but highly rewarding. Mostly strategy-oriented, getting through each of the unique and stylistic areas of the game is impossible without a carefully built party and well-planned attacks. The bosses are unique, challenging, and give quite a satisfying feeling when you finally land that killing blow and send those OP jerks straight into the abyss.
Aside from the gameplay, Darkest Dungeon has an interesting story, wonderful emersion, brilliant aesthetics, and a dark and gloomy atmosphere that contributes well to the game's themes of hopelessness and despair. Revolving mainly around the stress your heros recieve while marching through dank dungeons full of horrifying and powerful monsters, this game takes an interesting look on the whole "dungeon-crawling, monster-slaying" style of RPG that one typically sees. Darkest Dungeon is not about glory and heroism; it's about survival, and the occasional glimmer of hope in the darkness.
Overall: 9/10
PROS:
+Wonderful cameplay
+Great atmosphere
+Original concept
+Cool story, bro
CONS:
-Challenging and attention-requiring gameplay means casually playing DD is impossible
-Can be a bit to challenging, causing rage-quitting of the highest calibur
-Money is tight in this game, but so necessary that you end up scavenging for money almost more than you do acctually thrying to beat the bosses

I'll start by saying I'm really enjoying this game and don't regret getting it, however I don't reccomend buying it at full price in the state that it's in. If you can get it cheaper then go for it, provided you're a fan of EU/EW. XCOM 2 is more of the same, with a bit of different. There's a lot of good here and a lot of bad, but the bad is fixable, it's just that it shouldn't have been there to begin with.
Pros:
-The new base management and overworld stuff is pretty fun and in my opinion makes it feel like you're not just sitting and waiting for something to happen. Instead of having to try to manage a bunch of "feal levels", but only being able to affect one at a time, there's only one meter to worry about, and there are multiple ways to manage it. Having to make contact with different countries instead of having to prevent losing them gives you a bit more option as to how you approach things.
-The new/updated classes feel a lot more balanced and interesting. Each one having two distinct specializations makes your squad more diverse, however a couple of them do feel underpowered, specifically the scout and combat hacker trees.
-The weapon changes make things a lot less tedious in some aspects, but moreso in others. Pistols on the sharpshooter class are fantastic, they're decently powerful and give your sniper a way to fight in close quarters and able to attack/overwatch after moving. Being able to attack or move after reloading is just great, so taking away secondaries on all the other classes doesn't really hurt.
Meh:
-Turn timers, I know people are so divided on these which is why I put them in meh instead of cons, but I dislike them. I feel that they force you to play a certain way, even if you don't want to. I've had missions where I had to rush through enemies or else I wouldn't make it in time, causing me to risk my soldiers. There are already lots of mods to change how they work, whether it be increasing turns, reducing the amount of missions that use them, or outright getting rid of them.
-concealment adds a nice way to setup ambushes, however in most cases it doesn't work out like you think it would. This ties in to turn timers, in that the timers are counting down even while you're trying to set up your ambush. It's just not viable to try to tactically ambush the enemy when you have to get to the evac zone in 8 turns. Also having all enemies suddenly just know where you are when you break concealment can easily lead to you being surrounded if you're not careful.
Cons:
-Performance issues out the♥♥♥♥♥ Supposed to be patched.
-Glitches out the♥♥♥♥♥ Supposed to be patched.
-I don't know if it's a glitch or just poor design, but line of sight is just super wonky. I've had enemies attacking me through walls, stun lancers meleeing people through the floor above them, and worst of all, snakes pulling my guys through as many as three walls with no holes or windows in any of them, effectively dooming them.
-The difficulty curve is steep. Really steep. Within 5 missions I was fighting against armored enemies that could destroy my cover, incapacitate my troops, and almost kill them in one attack, while I was still researching t2 weapons and armor. Enemies pop up randomly one after another, giving you almost no time to adjust your strategy.
-Dodge. If that's not specific enough, most enemies have a chance to dodge, causing you to do greatly reduced damage. I know the discussion of rng has been done to death, but sometimes it feels like they just always dodge.
-Your soldiers' wounded level seems to be completely arbitrary. Soldiers that take 10% damage get gravely wounded and are out of the fight for a month to recover 2 hp. I've read of people having soldiers take over 50% damage and only being lightly wounded, but take 2 fall damage and be gravely wounded.
Hopefully they can patch the performance and glitches, with that I'd say it's worth it, but until then no. Other than that it's up to you whether these things bother you or not.

Anecdote (don't read this if you've decided against this game or don't care):
I had an entire team going into a battle against the Swine Prince. Healers, big damage, damage over time. Everything. The battle started with the Swine Prince and a little pig next to him. During the first turn he marked several people, who subsequently lost about half their health. So I killed the little pig, which afterward turned out to be a horrible idea. Every turn my heroes reminded me not to hurt the little pig while the Swine Prince was landing whole team attacks with big damage and stun. The art is incredible and the story draws you in like few other games i have experienced.

First of all, excuse this review for being the mess that it is...I'm not a game reviewer, so it's not going to be all polished and error free..I'm just a customer and mega-fan of the Fallout series that wanted to put my own review out there for people to read.
Anyways, Fallout 4 was a very mixed bag of things for me. The overall plot was weak as water, and most of the characters and locations you come across had little to no personality when compared to characters/locations in the previous games. I think the only real reason why I remember any of them is because I've put so many hours into Fallout 4, and because they became memes with how f***ing annoying they are. Minus Kellogg. Dude was an absolute boss.
Bethesda also made the decision to use the Creation engine one last time which lead to the game looking incredibly dated with some down right terrible textures in quite a few places (especially if you were stuck with the vanilla version on console when it was first released, like I was) I also thought that the environment was far too colorful and cartoonish for a Fallout game. Where I once felt dread, fear, and excitement going to new locations, I now mostly just get annoyed and tired of the monotony of what felt like many "copy and paste" sections of the game. (ESPECIALLY in the subways. Ugh.)
I also felt that the enemies are no longer intimidating or visceral or scary either. Super Mutants no longer feel like these disgusting mutated freaks that have lost everything that once made them human and now only exist to destroy what little humanity has managed to build back up after the war. Now they're just these goofy green guys (which you would know nothing about or how they were created if this was your first Fallout experience) with big annoying dogs that say dim-witted tough guy things. Thrilling, truly. This as I pointed out earleir just goes along with none of these characters having any sort of personality,
Those are my main gripes that I'll actually go into detail about, just because they were the aspects of the game that bothered me the most.
Other things that I didn't like;
-All of the DLC's sufferd from the same boring issues as the vanilla game. Far Habor and Nuka World were as wide as an ocean but as deep as a freaking puddle with glitches and bugs galore. What a nightmare. They over all felt incredibly lazy to me, especially the Wasteland Workshop(s). The modding community had already made a lot of Workshops components and did it FAR BETTER than Bethesda did in my opnion. I'll be honest and say that the only reason why I'm glad that the DLC'S came out is because it gave modders more content  to work with and make better. That's it.
-The people at your settlements with the exception of Sanctuary all reuse the same 2-3 voice actors and it's really freaking annoying and lazy. I'd rather they had no voices at all so I just don't have to hear them anymore.
-The people in the 4 original factions you can join are all pretty much as boring as the rest of the games characters, with a few exceptions. Deacon being my personal favorite.
-Lazy radiant quests make this game such a damn chore to play sometimes. It really just felt like Beth. just stopped giving a crap at some point and decided that quantity was more important than quality.
Now if you're reading this and you're thinking "well if the game sucks so bad, why have you played it so much then?" My answer is that I don't think it's a bad game over all. The mechanics in it are fine, and it's voice acted very well, and even though it's undeniably clunky (which again, mods have helped to fix), settlement building is a fun way to express your creative side and share it with the Fallout community. I just don't think it's a good FALLOUT game. With the introduction of the voiced main protagonist and no longer having the Karma system, you lose a lot of the role playing aspects that you had in the previous instalments. You could be a straight up a***hole and pick snarky lines of dialogue and do things like blowing up Megaton because it was obstructing the view of your fancy, shmancy hotel and be hated by everyone in the wasteland. Or you could be a goody two shoes (like I always am) and be revered as a saviour in everyones eyes and then be hunted down by bad guys because of your do-goody actions and squeeky image. You just don't get that in Fallout 4. If you want to go to Diamond City and kill a bunch of people and loot their corpses, just leave for 48 hours and come back and it'll be like nothing ever happened. That's just not fun... What happened Bethesda? What did we do to deserve this mess?
Well, that's pretty much all I've got to say about it. I just hope Bethesda goes back to Fallout's roots and re-discovers what made the series so great and stops trying to appeal to the lowest common denominators in the fan base.

Overall spectacular game.
If I had to describe it briefly, I would say that it"s turn-based Dark Souls.
Darkest Dungeon brings an entertaining mix of challenge and fun. The gameplay is extraordinarily difficult, but highly rewarding. Mostly strategy-oriented, getting through each of the unique and stylistic areas of the game is impossible without a carefully built party and well-planned attacks. The bosses are unique, challenging, and give quite a satisfying feeling when you finally land that killing blow and send those OP jerks straight into the abyss.
Aside from the gameplay, Darkest Dungeon has an interesting story, wonderful emersion, brilliant aesthetics, and a dark and gloomy atmosphere that contributes well to the game's themes of hopelessness and despair. Revolving mainly around the stress your heros recieve while marching through dank dungeons full of horrifying and powerful monsters, this game takes an interesting look on the whole "dungeon-crawling, monster-slaying" style of RPG that one typically sees. Darkest Dungeon is not about glory and heroism; it's about survival, and the occasional glimmer of hope in the darkness.
Overall: 9/10
PROS:
+Wonderful cameplay
+Great atmosphere
+Original concept
+Cool story, bro
CONS:
-Challenging and attention-requiring gameplay means casually playing DD is impossible
-Can be a bit to challenging, causing rage-quitting of the highest calibur
-Money is tight in this game, but so necessary that you end up scavenging for money almost more than you do acctually thrying to beat the bosses

Spiral Knights is a game developed by Three Rings and published by SEGA. It has a relaxing atmosphere and has intense combat. It prides itself on it's unique and vibrant artstyle which you can't help but love to bits. It's spawned some great fan art, too!
THE GOOD:
Spiral Knights does an excellent job at making you feel part of something, whether it be a guild, a team, or the game universe itself. The social features are really great. I've had no problem jumping into a game with a friend and bashing at some enemies in the depths of the clockworks! The combat is extremely satisfying and in terms of level structure and gameplay, I see that it takes some inspiration from the top-down Zelda games like A Link to the Past. The hub section of the game, Haven, is just beautiful to look at and is adorable. The art direction is especially admirable especially how it's presented as well. Boss fighs are well designed and a joy to fight and the story arc is as well pretty interesting. The soundtrack is especially epic. While it isn't on Skyrim levels of epic and style, it has it's own style of soundtrack which is an 8-bit/orchestra fusion which blends really well and has some unforgettable tracks. There's also a crafting system which is quite extensive and robust and presents quite a challenge. You need crafting to progress further to higher star items unless you want to pay for the next tier of items (which is overpriced as heck) which I find quite an interesting way to progress.
THE BAD:
I've been following the facebook community for some time and according to the fans, the developers have lately been pretty lazy only releasing reskins and expensive money stealing cosmetics. This has raised a bit of concern from me because the game is great and unique, I just don't want it to fall into recession and die out because of it. The developers need to work on bringing out new content to keep the game fresh and alive. I also heard from a friend of mine that Spiral Knights had the exact same Christmas event as last year. I just reckon that's a bit lazy from them.
THE CONCLUSION:
The game is unlike anything I've ever seen. The art style is the main part of it for me which has a great array of vibrant colours and retains a high contrast between them. The gameplay is solid, I can hack away at monsters for ages. Playing with friends is awesome, the soundtrack is great, crafting is cool, but the developers, Three Rings need to pick it up a little.
Spiral Knights earns a 9/10

To be honest, the plot arc of FO4 is not that great. This is a game Bethesda made where they thought they could rest on the laurels of their previous Fallout releases, and improve the graphics and some gameplay mechanics. But if you don't make good use of those improvements to tell a compelling story, you just wasted your technology. There is one milquetoast plot twist that you can see coming 100 miles away, and it occurs pretty early in the main quest. One can see how they could have made the plot more interesting going forward from that point, but they didn't. The existence of synths is never fully leveraged in the story, and the game could have / should have taken a few more pages out of Philip K.♥♥♥♥♥♥s stories that blur the line between human and artificial. This is only vaguely alluded to in FO4, and the player never directly experiences much of it. There is never any genuine confusion for the player (or a reason to care) who is human and who is not, or whether the non-humans deserve more to live than the humans do (the old "man is the most horrific animal of all" trope).
The game's success speaks for itself at this point, but for anyone who is going to be paying close attention to the plot, it's actually pretty disappointing. None of the DLCs ever fixed this, either.

A potentially great game stretched too thin for my tastes.
I found that there are two challenges to this game; difficulty and the time it takes to get gold.  The former was enjoyably demanding, the latter was a chore.
I enjoyed the first 30 hours but after accumulating 7 characters of final tier level I realised that in order for them to meet their full potential and have a good chance of beating the final dungeons they'd need to have afflictions removed, have good equipment and positive traits locked in.  Which takes money, LOTS of money.  Which means repeating dungeons, LOTS of dungeons, to the point of boredom.
I already felt slightly weary with the repetition when entering 30+ hour mark but carried on since I felt the end was in sight.  However, another 10 hours later, when I realised what would be required to complete the game, I felt like I was facing another 40+ hours - mainly grinding at lower level stuff.
It's a shame since there are so many cool things to do with the characters and so many classes to mess around with.   From experimenting with and increasing certain skill sets, to paying to permanently keep certain bonuses they have earned, it's an exciting prospect.  Doing this would really individualise them, add an extra layer of depth and greatly increase the RPG feel of it all but again, this costs money, TONS of money.  Cue even more grinding.
Simply put, I feel this could have been a great 40-50 hour game but the constant halt in progress to get obscene amounts of gold to heal, cure and upgrade the roster is so time consuming the game ends up artificially increasing its playtime beyond my interest and desire.  I'm guessing they made this decision in order to 'double down' on the difficulty but I find testing people's patience through grinding isn't a fun form of challenge.
Having said all that, if you pick it up cheap and get 30+ hours of enjoyment before repetition sets in then I guess that could be viewed as money well spent....just take into consideration that you won't finish the game in that time frame, beat the bosses nor see your characters and township reach their full potential.  Not even close. Whether that's a deal breaker is, of course, for you to decide.  If it isn't, then have fun :)

Leading up to Fallout 3's release, cynics were saying that it would just be "Oblivion with guns." Thankfully, they were wrong. Bethesda made a genuine effort to try and preserve at least some of what made Fallout "special" (different ways to tackle obstacles -- especially diplomatic options, stat and skill checks, etc.). Fallout 3 was a very different game compared to Fallout 1 & 2, but at least they tried to keep some connective tissue there. Fast forward to the release of Fallout 4, and Bethesda decided to water down all of these Fallout-y gameplay elements drastically, which unfortunatley means that it really now is just "Skyrim with guns."  As a Bethesda game, it's sufficient (if uninspired), but as a Fallout game, Bethesda really dropped the ball. If Fallout will be used as a cash cow to be milked between Elder Scrolls games moving forward, then this is where I get off. Plus, I could go on about how the writing and animations are atrocious (this game has by far the worst story in a Fallout game), but Bethesda already knows that. They just don't care.

A lot of reviewers have already said what needs to be said.
The voice acting, the game's story, the game theme, all of it is very high quality. However, the game artificially lengthens its playtime by throwing too many punishing mechanics against you, with too many random elements.
As one example of a problematic random element, nailing a critical hit is massively damaging, and while it can feel satisfying for your group to instant kill a target from a lucky dice roll (along with cool narrative from the narrator), the enemy can do the same to your characters (especially with chained criticals), which strips you of any tactical defensive options you'd want to employ. For this reason, it's not really a question of "if" a character will die, but "when" the character will die. You can't get too attached to your characters like you do in X-Com in Ironman mode, for example, thinking there's a chance they might survive. You actually have to grind parties to their death over and over and over and over again until you amass enough gold to upgrade your town to the point that you can then begin creating an endgame group (or try to) after another long grind of amassing wealth with suicide runs.

The best way to describe Starbound is Terraria in space.  What was done in Terraria is expanded at least ten fold in Starbound.
Players choose a race, choose from a starting set of clothes, progress through tech tiers, and fight bosses.  As of 2014-02-22, the first four tech tiers a locked until you kill a boss.  There are rumors of a fifth boss, but it has not been implemented as of this review.  It is my hope that every tech tier will eventually have a boss to defeat.
Just like Terraria, players can get items and equipment from friends.  There are no equipment requirements, so this can significantly boost your power level without passing the boss gate.  This is both good and bad, since progression is a huge incentive.  Being given tier ten (aka max tier) gear removes that sense of accomplishment.
Unlike Terraria, players are free to travel between 12.667 quadrillion planets.
reports this number is expected to reach 422.22 quadrillion upon full release.  Planets are currently divided between five sectors (alpha, beta, gamma, delta, and X).  Each sector is designed for a certain tech tier:  A is 1, B is 2, G is 3, D is 4, X is 5-10.  Players will notice the mineral content and enemy strengths change according to these tiers.
One criticism of Starbound vs. Terraria.  In Terraria, you had the one world to explore.  You could build a great fortress or palace as your home base.  In Starbound, you may set a home planet to do this, warping directly to the home planet from your ship, no matter what planet the ship is currently orbiting.  In my opinion, the best replacement to Terraria’s home base is a mod like
Want Star Trek’s Enterprise?  Star War’s Death Star?  Firefly’s Serenity?  Build and design to your heart’s content!
If you’re not sure about Starbound, I encourage you to pick up Terraria.  You should be to pick it up for $10 (or less during sales).  If you enjoy it, Starbound is definitely worthy in its current state and will only get better as more features are added.  Starbound is still subject to character wipes, but 12 quadrillion planets provide plenty of variability in gameplay for each mandatory restart.

Disclaimer, No. 1: This review is whole-heartedly biased because I think this game is excellent. It may also wander significatly, and slightly increases your risk of dying in a car accident (for reasons wholly unknown to science).
Disclaimer, No. 2: This game allows you to create facimilies of your friends and family; Mutons will proceed to butcher those friends and family without hesitation, mercy, or remorse. It also allows you to put friends and family into assasination missions (really you're supposed to capture them, but I can't quite resist the temptation to put a grenade at my brother's feet).
Disclaimers aside: I agree with the majority of complaints about this game; I agree that they exist, anyways. I don't think that they ruin the game, however, and for a simple reason: XCOM 2 is whatever you want it to be (unless you want it to be a shooter, in which case, you're out of luck).
XCOM 2 is a very focused game. It's clear that there was a tone and pace that the developers wanted to set, and they did so perfectly; XCOM 2 is frantic and breathless, and absolutly phenomenal at rushing the player along. Sometimes, though you don't want to rush, and (very, very fortunatly) that's fine: Because you have access to the game's .ini files.
If you don't want the tight time limits (which I agree could be a turn or three longer) you don't have to have the tight time limits. If you don't like the way a particular weapon is balenced because it interdicts a particualar personal strategy, or just doesn't seem fair, you're perfectly capable of nerfing or buffing it yourself. While yes, I know, the developers shouldn't leave the fine tuning of their game to the customer, I'm very greatful that they did. Now we can balence the game the way we want, or completly unbalance it instead.
There are some questionable design choices at the heart of XCOM 2, but there are also a miriad number of ways to circumvent those design choices, and play the game your own way, at your own pace, because of other design choices that I've mentioned before and agree with thoroughly.
On another note: While I would like slighly more time during missions and on the global map, XCOM 2 is a solid, absolutly worthwhile game, even without mods or tweaks to timers, stats, and miscelenea.
On a different note: I've encountered a few timing bugs, but otherwise performance has been smooth. I have the bare minimum in the graphics department (Intel Iris Pro) and I'm still able to play on medium graphics, with not-horrible framrate.
Short Version: XCOM 2 is good. You'll like it if you liked the previous games. Tweak it if the previous statement proves horrifically false.
